If it still cannot tell, the sheet stays and gives you four buttons:
- **Check again**: asks Zeller again.
- **Customer WAS charged**: only if you have **seen it approved on the terminal or the Zeller dashboard**. It records the payment as paid by card.
- **Customer was NOT charged**: only if you have checked and it is not there. It lets you charge again.
- **Close**: leaves the question open.

Both of the middle buttons ask you to confirm, and your name is saved with the decision. Until an unknown payment on this sale is settled, **Card** refuses with *A previous card payment has no result yet. Resolve it before charging again.* Cash and gift cards still work.

### Reader not ready
If the terminal cannot be used, a **Reader** sheet says what is wrong, with **Retry** and **Close**. The messages are:
- *Terminal not paired - open Diagnostics ▸ Zeller ▸ Setup.* The terminal has never been paired with this iPad (or the app was reinstalled).
- *No internet - card payments need a connection. Cash still works.*
- *Terminal is busy. Please wait and try again.* Or *The terminal is serving another register.*
- *Can’t reach the terminal - check its power and Wi‑Fi.* Or *Couldn’t connect to the terminal.*

If the reader is not ready you also see **Reader issue** in red at the top right of the Payment screen, and a **Reader issue** notice is added to your notifications.

To check or fix the reader, open **More ▸ Support & diagnostics**. Under **Zeller reader** you have **Check reader**, **Setup (pair terminal)**, and **Test purchase $1.00** with **Refund the $1.00 test** afterwards. After reinstalling the app you must pair the terminal again.

For a step-by-step reader troubleshooting guide, see [[fix/reader]].

### Good to know
- Card amounts are never rounded.
- A card payment can be refunded from the terminal if you cancel a part-paid sale (see [[pay]]).
- The register will not lock, and staff cannot be switched, while a card payment is waiting.
sections.deep:
### Why a card payment is never repeated by accident
Every card attempt gets its own reference, made from the sale's id and the attempt number. The POS saves the attempt on the iPad **before** it tells the terminal anything, then asks the terminal to take the payment. If the answer is ever unclear, it looks the payment up by that reference instead of guessing. That is how it can tell "the customer paid just as you pressed Cancel" from "nothing happened".

The same care explains the rule about unknown results: charging again before you know could take the money twice, so the POS blocks it until the first attempt is settled.

### What counts as "unknown"
The POS treats a result as unknown when it cannot be sure no money moved: the connection dropped after the terminal had started, the terminal timed out, the bank's answer could not be read, or a reversal was still pending. A plain decline before the card was processed is **not** unknown, and neither is a failure to start (no internet, not paired).

### The kinds of decline
Each bank or terminal code is put in one of four groups, and the message follows from the group:
- **Try another card**: insufficient funds, expired, lost or stolen, blocked, over the limit, not supported.
- **The customer can fix it**: wrong PIN, signature problem, card not read, card needs inserting.
- **Try again**: a bank, network or terminal hiccup.
- **Contact Zeller**: the merchant or terminal set-up is wrong. Retrying will not help.
A code the POS does not know shows the terminal's own wording, or *Declined (code …)*. The **Not approved** sheet always offers **Try card again**, whatever the group, so use the message to decide.

### Fees
Zeller's result does not include a fee, so the POS works one out. The rates are in **Settings ▸ Payments**: **Card-present fee %** (1.4% unless changed) and **Keyed / card-not-present fee %** (1.7%). A manually keyed or online-style payment uses the keyed rate. The fee is kept on the payment as an estimate. A refund does not return the original fee.

### Offline and the reader's state
The POS asks the terminal whether it is ready when the app starts, and again about every minute while it is not ready, so **Reader issue** clears by itself once the problem is fixed. A card payment needs the internet; cash and gift cards are separate, so cash always works.

### Cancelling a sale that already has a card payment
Choosing **Refund & cancel** on a part-paid sale refunds each card payment through the terminal, one after another. If a refund does not complete you see **Refund did not complete**, nothing is cancelled, and the problem is written to the history so you can follow it up. Check the terminal before trying again.
sections.advanced:
### What happens when you tap Card
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[runCard in Pay.tsx] --> B{buttons locked or an unknown attempt on this sale}
  B -->|unknown attempt| C[Payment status unknown sheet]
  B -->|no| D{terminal ready}
  D -->|no| E[checkReader in zellerBridge.tsx]
  E -->|still no| F[Reader sheet]
  D -->|yes| G[attemptRef then onStarted saves the attempt as started]
  E -->|ready| G
  G --> H[startCharge in zeller.ts calls terminal.purchase]
  H --> I[normalise turns the SDK result into a PaymentResult]
  I -->|APPROVED| J[cardTender then addTender]
  I -->|DECLINED| K[Not approved sheet]
  I -->|CANCELLED| L[back to idle]
  I -->|NOT_READY| F
  I -->|UNKNOWN| M[recheck: reconcile up to 6 times 4 s apart]
  M -->|approved| J
  M -->|declined or cancelled| K
  M -->|no answer| C
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The flow, sheets and strip | `runCard`, `recheck`, `manualResolve` in `src/screens/Pay.tsx` |
| Which states may draw a sheet | `showsOwnSheet`, `showsWaitingStrip`, `lockPayButtons` in `src/lib/payUi.ts` |
| Talking to the SDK | `startCharge`, `startRefund`, `reconcile`, `normalise`, `describeEvent` in `src/lib/zeller.ts` |
| One terminal for the whole app | `ZellerRoot`, `getTerminal`, `checkReader`, `pairReader` in `src/zellerBridge.tsx` |
| Code to message | `RESPONSE_CODES`, `lookupResponse` in `src/lib/responseCodes.ts` |
| Fees | `feeFor`, `feeRateFor` in `src/lib/fees.ts`; `cardTender` in `src/lib/saleBuilder.ts` |
| Pairing, test purchase, attempts list | `src/screens/Diagnostics.tsx` |
| Saved attempts | `Attempt` in `src/state/store.ts` (`pos.attempts`) |
| Locking while waiting | `paymentActive` in `src/lib/screensaver.ts`, used by `lockDecision` in `src/lib/posLock.ts` and by staff switching in `src/lib/staffAuth.ts` |

The SDK returns errors instead of throwing them. `normalise` turns either kind of result into one of five outcomes: `APPROVED`, `DECLINED`, `CANCELLED`, `UNKNOWN` or `NOT_READY`, and nothing outside `zeller.ts` reads a raw SDK result. A network or connection failure is `NOT_READY` when the terminal had not started, and `UNKNOWN` once it had.

`startCharge` does one more thing before it returns. If the result is cancelled or unknown, or a decline arrived after the terminal had started processing, it calls `reconcile`, which looks the reference up with `getTransactions`. An approved match turns the result into `APPROVED`. That lookup is what makes Cancel safe.

The attempt's status moves `started`, then `approved`, `declined`, `cancelled`, `unknown` or `resolved`. A **started** attempt keeps `paymentActive` true for five minutes, which is what blocks locking and staff switching; an attempt left at **started** by a closed app stops blocking after that. The waiting state itself is not saved, so reopening Payment shows the buttons again, but an `unknown` attempt on the sale still blocks **Card** through `blockedByUnknown`.

Events are written to the history CSV with `csv.event`: `declined`, `cancelled`, `unknown_payment`, `unknown_resolved`, `refund_failed` and `void`.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **Card button does nothing.** The amount is $0 (`runCard` returns when it is 0 or less), the buttons are locked by a waiting card phase, or an `unknown` attempt exists for this sale.
- **"Reader issue" that will not clear.** In More ▸ Support & diagnostics tap **Check reader**: it calls `initialise` on the terminal. `Setup Required` means pair it. `Network Failure` shows as *Reader offline - no internet*.
- **The customer was charged but the sale shows no card payment.** It is an `unknown` attempt: check **Card attempts (this device)** in Support & diagnostics (the last eight, with their reference and who resolved them) and look for the same reference in the Zeller dashboard. The reference is the sale id followed by the attempt number.
- **A decline message is vague.** The code is not in `RESPONSE_CODES`, so the SDK's own text is shown. Add it there if you want better wording.
- **The reader says busy.** *Paired Device Busy* means another register is using the terminal. Only one register can charge at a time.
- **Tests.** `tests/lib.test.ts` covers the response codes, fees, `normalise`, and `startCharge` (approve; a cancel after processing that still approves through `reconcile`; a timeout that stays unknown; a decline that keeps the cart) and `startRefund`. `tests/payui.test.ts` covers which states may draw a sheet.

pages.title: Paying by cash
pages.summary: Taking cash by tapping the notes and coins handed over, giving change from the drawer, and what to do when the drawer cannot make the change.
pages.lead: Cash is taken by tapping the notes and coins the customer hands over. The POS works out the change, shows which notes and coins to take from the drawer, and keeps a record of what is in the drawer as it goes.

sections.basic:
### Taking cash
1. On the **Payment** screen tap **Cash** (**Pay with cash** in Simple and Minimal modes).
2. The **Cash received** sheet opens. At the top it shows **Due**, the amount the customer owes in cash.
3. Tap each note and coin the customer hands you. Each tap adds one. The number under the note or coin shows how many you have tapped, and **Received** shows the total.
4. The line under **Due** tells you where you are:
   - **Tap what the customer hands over**: nothing tapped yet.
   - **Short by $…** (red): they have not given enough.
   - **Exact** (green): the right amount.
   - **Change to give: $…** (green): they gave too much and you owe change. It turns red if the drawer cannot make that change (see below).

```screen
title: Cash received
text: Due $28.50
text: Change to give: $1.50
label: Notes
tile: $50
tile: !1 $20 | × 1
tile: $10
label: Coins
tile: $2 | × 1
tile: 50c
tile: 20c
button: Undo
primary: Next: give $1.50 change
note: Each tap adds one note or coin, and the count under it shows how many you have tapped.
```

### The tap pad
- **Add / Remove** switch: choose **Remove** to take notes or coins off what you have tapped. Removing something you have not tapped says *None of that to remove.*
- **Each tap** (**×1**, **×5**, **×10**): how many one tap adds, handy for rolls of coins.
- **Undo** takes back your last tap and tells you what it removed and the new total. **Start over** clears everything.
- Notes are $100, $50, $20, $10 and $5. Coins are $2, $1, 50c, 20c, 10c and 5c.

### What happens next
- **Exact:** tap **Take cash**. The payment is added and, if nothing remains, the sale finishes.
- **Short:** you can ask for more, or tap **Take $… as part payment**. The cash is recorded as a payment of what they gave, and the rest is paid another way. On a split bill the screen instead offers to move the shortfall into a later payment, spread it, or go back and change the split. See [[pay/split-and-part]].
- **Change to give:** tap **Next: give $… change**. The **Give change** screen shows **Take from the drawer** with the notes and coins to hand back.
  - **Gave this** confirms you handed over exactly that.
  - **I'll give different notes and coins** lets you tap what you really gave. The total must match the change owed.
  - **Show another way** appears only when Smart change is on in Settings ▸ Payments and there is more than one good option. It steps through them. See [[cash/smart-change]].
  - **Back** returns to the notes you tapped.

### When the drawer cannot make the change
A red box says **Can't make $… change** and **Next** is greyed out. See [[cash/change]] for what that means and how each option is found, or [[fix/cant-make-change]] for what to do at the till. It lists what could work:
- **Ask for less:** take a smaller part of what they handed over and give the rest straight back. Tap **Use that smaller handover** to do it.
- **Cash $… + the rest another way:** take part of the bill in cash (the most the drawer can make change for) and put the remainder on card or another method.
- **Or take the full amount by card.**

If the box says **No cash in the ledger**, the drawer was never opened or counted, so the POS has no idea what is in it. Open the drawer from More ▸ Cash drawer first. See [[cash/open-close]].

If you can see the drawer really does have the change and the record is out of date, tap **The drawer has it (ledger is out of date)**. You then tap the notes and coins you give. Fix the record later with **Correct contents** or **Count & close** in the cash drawer. See [[cash/open-close]].

### Cash rounding
If **Cash rounding (5c)** is on in Settings ▸ Payments, the cash due on the **last** payment is rounded to the nearest 5c. 1c and 2c round down, 3c and 4c round up. So $10.02 is due as $10.00 and $10.03 as $10.05. Earlier payments in a split are never rounded.

### Free sales
If the total is $0.00 the only button is **Complete $0.00 sale**.

### Cancelling a sale that has cash in it
If you back out of a part-paid sale, the app asks you to collect any exact change previously given and return the exact notes and coins originally received. Follow the prompts and confirm the denominations physically exchanged; cancellation does not use the change optimizer.
sections.deep:
### Where the change comes from
The change is made from the notes and coins in the drawer record **plus what the customer just handed over**. So the customer's own notes can go straight back as change, and a drawer with no small notes can still change a $20 if the customer handed over a $10 and a $5 as well. Among all the exact ways to make the change, the POS picks the one with the fewest pieces, which is quickest to count out. With **Smart change** on it picks the way that leaves the drawer best stocked for the next sales instead (see [[cash/smart-change]]). The full story of how change is found is on [[cash/change]], and you can check a customer's notes before taking them with [[cash/check-change]].

### How rounding is worked out
Rounding is applied to the cash **due**, not to what was handed over, and only when that cash payment clears the whole of what remains. The sale keeps the real amount and records the rounding separately, so receipts and reports can show it. Rounding down means the customer paid up to 2c less than the bill, rounding up means up to 2c more. If the cash is only part of the bill, nothing is rounded.

### Short payments are not change
If the customer hands over less than is due, the payment is recorded as the amount handed over, with no change. That is what **Take $… as part payment** does.

### What each button writes to the drawer record
| You tap | Notes and coins in | Change out |
|---|---|---|
| **Take cash** (exact) | recorded | none |
| **Take $… as part payment** | recorded | none |
| **Gave this** (suggested or manually counted) | recorded | recorded |
| **Cash refund** (suggested or manually counted) | none | recorded |
| **Cancel part-paid sale** | exact original tender is removed | previously given change is collected back |

### The two ways round a drawer that cannot make change
- **Ask for less** looks for the smallest amount you could keep from what they handed over that still covers the bill and whose change the drawer **can** make. Example: the drawer has one $5, the customer hands you $20, $10 and $5 for a $25 bill. Keep the $20 and $5 and hand the $10 straight back, so no change is needed at all.
- **Part in cash** looks for the largest cash amount below the bill, in 5c steps, whose change can be made. Example: the drawer has one $20, the customer hands you a $50 for a $37 bill. The $13 change cannot be made, but $30 in cash works ($20 change from the drawer), leaving $7 for card.

### The record can drift
The record is only as good as what is tapped. It lives on each iPad separately. See [[cash]]. Count & close and Correct contents are the ways it gets reset or corrected.
sections.advanced:
### From Cash to a payment
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Cash button in Pay.tsx] --> B[CashSheet receive step]
  B --> C{cashStatus of due and received}
  C -->|short| D[Take as part payment]
  C -->|exact| E[Take cash]
  C -->|change| F{planChange from drawer plus received}
  F -->|exact| G[GiveCash change step]
  F -->|impossible| H[handBackOptions and partCashOption]
  H --> G
  G --> I[onTake with received and given]
  D --> I
  E --> I
  I --> J[takeCash in Pay.tsx]
  J --> K[cashTender builds the Tender]
  J --> L[postCashSale writes the ledger]
  K --> M[addTender]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The sheet and its two steps | `CashSheet` in `src/screens/CashSheet.tsx` |
| The change step (also used for cash refunds) | `GiveCash`, `GiveCashSheet` in `src/screens/CashSheet.tsx` |
| The tap pad | `DenomPad` in `src/ui/DenomPad.tsx`; the maths in `src/lib/cashLedger.ts` |
| Due, short, exact, change | `cashDue`, `cashStatus` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Which notes and coins to give | `planChange` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts`; `planChangeSmart` in `src/lib/changeScore.ts` when Smart change is on |
| Ask for less, part in cash | `handBackOptions`, `partCashOption` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Building the payment | `cashTender` in `src/lib/saleBuilder.ts`; `takeCash` in `src/screens/Pay.tsx` |
| Writing and reversing the drawer record | `postCashSale`, `recordCancelledCashTender` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Rounding | `roundCash` in `src/lib/money.ts` |
| Empty drawer check | `ledgerEmpty` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |

### The payment record
A cash payment (a `Tender` of kind `cash`) has these fields:
- `amountCents`: what was applied to the bill. For a settling payment this is the amount due **before** rounding. For a short payment it is what was handed over.
- `tenderedCents` and `changeCents`: what was handed over and what went back.
- `roundingCents`: the rounded due minus the amount (can be negative).
- `cashIn` and `cashOut`: the notes and coins received and given.

`cashTender` settles when the amount handed over is at least the due amount (rounded if rounding is on). Rounding is only passed in when `takeCash` sees `isFinal`: the payment is for everything that remains and it is not a part-cash amount (`applyCents` is not set). The sheet shows the same rounded amount because it gets it from `cashDue`.

`takeCash` writes the denominations received and given to the drawer record. On a cancelled sale, the cashier collects back the previously recorded change and returns exactly the originally received denominations; `recordCancelledCashTender` logs that physical exchange.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **Next is greyed out and the box says Can't make change.** `planChange` found no exact combination from the drawer plus what was received. Check the record in More ▸ Cash drawer.
- **The drawer record differs from the physical drawer.** The denominations entered may not match what was physically exchanged. Use Correct contents or Count & close.
- **Rounded amount looks wrong.** Check Settings ▸ Payments ▸ Cash rounding (5c). It only applies when this payment clears the remaining amount.
- **Show another way is missing.** Smart change is off, there is only one way to make the change, or the search was cut short.
- **Tests.** `tests/cashsale.test.ts` (status, change, ask for less, part in cash, ledger entries), `tests/cashledger.test.ts` (the tap pad and ledger), `tests/changescore.test.ts` (Smart change), `tests/sale.test.ts` (building cash payments).

pages.title: Paying with a gift card
pages.summary: Scanning or typing a gift card code to pay, what the balance screen says, why the card is charged straight away, and what the messages mean.
pages.lead: A gift card pays part or all of a sale. The balance lives on the card in Shopify, so a card works on any register as long as the iPad is online.

sections.basic:
### Taking a gift card payment
1. On the **Payment** screen tap **Gift card** (**Pay with a gift card** in Simple and Minimal modes).
2. The **Check gift card** sheet opens. Tap **Scan** and scan the QR code on the card or receipt, or type the code into **Code** and tap **Check**. **Check** stays greyed out until at least four characters are typed.
3. The sheet shows the card (**Card ••••** and its last four characters), its balance, and whether it is **Active** or **Disabled**. It may also say **code could not be verified** or **expires** with a date.
4. Tap **Use as payment**. This button only appears when the card is **Active** and has a balance.
5. The amount is taken from the card straight away and the payment is added to the list as **Gift card**.

```screen
title: Check gift card
text: Scan or type the code on the card.
input: Code | ABD2-4EF6
button: Scan
label: Result
row: Card •••• 4EF6
row: Balance | $15.00
row: Status | Active
primary: !1 Use as payment
note: The amount is the balance or the next payment amount, whichever is less.
```

The amount taken is the card's balance or the next payment amount, whichever is **less**. If the balance is smaller than what is owed, the rest stays under **Remaining** and you take it another way.

### Typing and scanning the code
- Letters and numbers only. Capitals, spaces and dashes do not matter.
- A scanned gift card QR carries a prefix that starts with `shopify-giftcard`. You never have to remove it, the POS strips it for you.

### Messages
- **No gift card found for that code.** Check the code and try again. Look at the card or receipt rather than guessing.
- **Lookup failed** with a reason: usually no internet. Gift cards need a connection, cash does not.
- **Disabled** next to the balance: the card has been switched off in Shopify. There is no **Use as payment** button. Ask the owner.
- **code could not be verified:** the card was not made by this POS, so the POS can only partly check it. It can still be used if **Active**.
- **Gift card could not be charged** with a reason: Shopify refused. Nothing was taken from the card and nothing was added to the sale.

### Good to know
- A gift card is never rounded and has no card fee.
- You cannot pay for a gift card with itself. A gift card sold in the same sale does not exist until that sale is paid.
- If you cancel a part-paid sale, the money **is** put back on the gift card automatically. The POS credits the card once, with a "POS cancel" note on the transaction, so running it again does not double-credit.
- To check a balance without paying, use the **Check gift card** option in the cart menu or More ▸ Gift cards.
For a balance check, redemption history, and the difference between a card QR and a claim QR, see [[gift/check-redeem]].
sections.deep:
### Why the card is charged first
The balance is taken off the card the moment you tap **Use as payment**, before the sale is finished. That stops two registers spending the same balance at once. The POS charges the card, and only if Shopify agrees does it add the payment to the sale. If you cancel the sale afterwards, the POS puts the money back on the card with a "POS cancel" note.

### How a code is found
Shopify can only search for gift cards by their last four characters. The POS searches that way, then looks at a hidden note on each candidate that holds a fingerprint of the full code, made when the POS created the card. A match is a verified card. If none match, the POS accepts a card **only** when exactly one candidate has no POS note at all and the code has eight or more characters, and then shows **code could not be verified**. Anything else is **No gift card found**.

### What the sale records
The payment keeps the card's Shopify id and the code. On the Shopify order it appears as a **Gift card** payment of that amount, with only the last four characters of the code stored. Refunds to the original gift card use the same id.

### Expiry
The sheet shows an expiry date but the POS does not check it. If Shopify refuses an expired card you see **Gift card could not be charged** with Shopify's reason.
sections.advanced:
### From Gift card to a payment
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Gift card button in Pay.tsx] --> B[GiftCheckSheet in sheets.tsx]
  B --> C[stripGiftPrefix on typed or scanned text]
  C --> D[lookupGiftCard in giftcards.ts]
  D -->|none| E[No gift card found]
  D -->|card| F{enabled and balance above 0}
  F -->|no| G[no Use as payment button]
  F -->|yes| H[useGift in Pay.tsx]
  H --> I[debitGiftCard]
  I -->|error| J[Gift card could not be charged]
  I -->|ok| K[addTender with kind gift_card]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The sheet (also used by Check gift card) | `GiftCheckSheet` in `src/screens/sheets.tsx` |
| Taking the payment | `useGift` in `src/screens/Pay.tsx` |
| Code cleaning | `stripGiftPrefix`, `normaliseCode` in `src/lib/giftCode.ts` |
| Finding and charging the card | `lookupGiftCard`, `debitGiftCard` in `src/lib/shopify/giftcards.ts` |
| The payment record | `giftCardId`, `giftCardCode` on `Tender` in `src/lib/types.ts` |
| Shopify order and stored code | `GATEWAY` in `src/lib/shopify/orderModel.ts`; `encodeTender` in `src/lib/saleCodec.ts` |
| Refunds to a gift card | `src/lib/refundFlow.ts` |

`useGift` takes the smaller of the card balance and the current target, charges it with a note naming the sale, then adds the payment with the cleaned code. It does not touch the cash drawer record.

### Receipts
The receipt built straight after the sale uses the full code in the payment line, as **Gift card** followed by the code. A receipt rebuilt later from the Shopify order only knows the last four characters. Only the last four are stored on the order.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **Use as payment is missing.** The card is disabled or has a zero balance (`GiftCheckSheet` checks both).
- **A card the customer swears is valid is not found.** More than one card ends in the same four characters and none carries this POS's fingerprint, or the code was typed wrongly.
- **Charged but the sale shows no gift card payment.** The charge succeeded and the app stopped before `addTender`. Look at the card's history in Shopify.
- **Tests.** `tests/giftcode.test.ts` (prefix and cleaning), `tests/lookup.test.ts` (scanning a gift QR), `tests/sale.test.ts` (the stored code and refund split).

pages.title: Receipts, QR codes and email
pages.summary: The Receipt sheet after a sale, how a customer gets their receipt (QR, email, text, share), what the receipt page shows, tax invoices, and what to do when a receipt is not published yet.
pages.lead: When a sale is paid, the **Receipt** sheet opens so you can give the customer their receipt. In normal use that is a link to a web page, which the customer opens by scanning a QR code or from a message.

sections.basic:
### The Receipt sheet
It opens by itself the moment the last payment is taken. At the top you see the total, **Sale complete**, and the Shopify order number when it is already known. If the customer paid cash and got change, **Change $…** shows in large type, so you can say it out loud.

```screen
title: Sale complete
sub: Order #1001
text: Total $28.50
text: Change $1.50
button: Show QR code
button: Email link
button: Text link
button: Share…
primary: No receipt
note: "No receipt" clears the cart for the next customer, even after you have sent a link.
```

There is no close button and you cannot swipe the sheet away. You finish with **No receipt**, which clears the cart for the next customer. The button keeps that name even after you have sent a link, so tap it when you are done.

### If the receipt page is set up
The buttons are:
- **Show QR code**: a QR code the customer scans with their phone camera. The page shows the itemised receipt, with **Download PDF**, **Save as image** and **Print**. **Back** returns to the buttons.
- **Email link**: opens the iPad's Mail app with the link already written. If the sale has a customer with an email address, it is filled into **To**. Otherwise you type it.
- **Text link**: the same, in Messages, with the customer's mobile if there is one.
- **Share…**: the iPad share sheet, for AirDrop or any other app.
- **No receipt**.

Selling a gift card adds a few extra buttons for that card (a QR for the customer to claim it, and a QR for scanning it at a register). They are covered with the gift card pages.

### If the receipt page is not set up
The buttons read **Email receipt**, **Text receipt**, **Share…** and **No receipt**. What is sent is a plain text receipt: shop name, date and time, the order number, each line with its price, discounts, the total, how it was paid, and *Thank you!*. There is no QR code, PDF or tax invoice. The receipt page is set up in Settings ▸ Receipts. The **Receipts** row in Settings says **Not set up** until a server address is entered. For configuration, see [[settings/receipts]].

### What the customer sees
The page lists your business name, ABN, address and contact details, then the receipt number (it looks like `R-1A2B3C4D`), the order number, the date and time, and who served them. Below that are the items with any discounts, then the totals, then how it was paid. Card payments show the card type, the last four digits, the approval code and the terminal reference. Cash shows what was handed over and the change. If your return policy is filled in, it is at the bottom.

Before downloading, the customer can type a **Billed to (name)** and a **Buyer ABN (optional)** on the page. These are only used for that download. Nothing they type is sent anywhere or saved.

### Tax invoice or receipt
- If **Registered for GST** is on in Settings ▸ Receipts, the document is titled **Tax invoice** and shows *Total includes GST of $…*. Gift card lines are left out of the GST.
- If it is off, the document is titled **Receipt** and has no GST lines.
- A refund is titled **Refund receipt**, or **Adjustment note (refund)** when GST is on, and says **Total refunded**.

Check the wording with your accountant. The page says so itself in the settings.

### Giving a receipt later
- Transactions ▸ pick the sale ▸ **New receipt** opens the same sheet again. Use it when a customer asks after they have left.
- **Share receipt text** on the same screen shares the plain text version.
- Orders ▸ pick the order ▸ **Receipt** also works, but the page it makes is plainer. See Deep.

### If something looks wrong
- **Not published yet. It goes live when this iPad can reach the receipt server.** appears under the QR code when the iPad could not upload the receipt (usually no internet). Show the QR code anyway: the page appears on its own once the iPad reconnects. Tell the customer to refresh in a minute.
- **Receipt not found** on the customer's phone: they scanned before the upload finished, or the iPad is offline. Ask them to try again shortly.
- **Receipt page not published** in Notifications: the iPad has no receipt server address or secret, or the server turned the upload down. See Deep, then fix Settings ▸ Receipts.
- **Could not open that app** after tapping **Email link** or **Text link**: the iPad has no Mail account, or cannot send texts. Use **Share…** instead.
sections.deep:
### Why a link and not a printed slip
One page holds the Shopify order lines **and** the card details from Zeller, so it works as the single record for tax. Because it is a web page, the customer can download a PDF or an image, and the same link works if they need it again.

### The link never changes
Each receipt's address is made from the sale itself (an unguessable 80-bit code), so the link for a sale is always the same. Uploading again overwrites the same page rather than making a second one. Search engines are told to ignore the pages, and they never expire, because they are tax records.

### When the page is published
It can happen up to four times, and all of them are safe to repeat:
1. As soon as the Receipt sheet opens, so the QR code usually works straight away.
2. When you tap **Show QR code**, which waits for the upload before showing the code. If the upload fails, the code still shows, with the note above.
3. In the background queue (the same one that sends the sale to Shopify), **before** the Shopify order is made, so a customer scanning within seconds still finds a page.
4. In the queue again **after** the order exists, so the page carries the Shopify order number.

If the server cannot be reached (offline, or a server error), the queue item stays where it is and only the receipt step is repeated later. This never holds up the Shopify order.

If the server address or secret is missing, or the server refuses the receipt, the queue shows **Receipt page not published**, and then **gives up on that sale's receipt**. It does not retry, because retrying cannot fix a wrong setting. After fixing Settings ▸ Receipts, open the sale in Transactions and tap **New receipt**: that uploads it again.

### Gift card payments
Today a gift card payment shows as **Gift card** followed by the code on a receipt built straight after the sale. A receipt rebuilt later only knows the last four characters. See [[pay/gift-card]].

### Cash rounding on the receipt
The payment amount on a receipt includes any cash rounding, so the payment line matches what the customer actually handed over less change. Rounding also shows as its own **Rounding** line in the totals, and **Subtotal** only appears when there is a discount, rounding or tip to explain.

### Receipts made from an order, not from the sale
Transactions ▸ **New receipt** on a sale made on this iPad uses the saved sale, so it is identical to the original. A sale from another register is rebuilt from its Shopify order. That works, but it has no discount names, no tip and no staff name, and because it uses the same link it **replaces** the original page with the plainer one. Orders ▸ **Receipt** rebuilds from the order too, but makes a **different** link, and it shows each line at its original price with no discount row. Both still show the right total.

### Business details are copied at upload time
Your name, ABN, address and the GST switch are read from Settings ▸ Receipts every time a receipt is uploaded. If you change them later and then reopen an old sale's **New receipt**, that page is rewritten with the new details.
sections.advanced:
### From a finished sale to a page
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[recordSale queues the sale] --> B[runItem in sync.ts]
  B --> C{receipts on and step not done}
  C -->|yes| D[uploadReceipt before the Shopify order]
  C -->|no| E[create the Shopify order]
  D --> E
  E --> F[uploadReceipt again with the order number]
  G[ReceiptPrompt opens] --> H[uploadReceipt in an effect]
  I[Show QR code] --> J[uploadReceipt then show the QR]
  D --> K[PUT /api/r/id on the Worker]
  F --> K
  H --> K
  J --> K
  K --> L[validate then store in KV]
  M[Customer opens /r/id] --> N[Worker reads KV and renders the page]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The sheet and its buttons | `ReceiptPrompt` in `src/screens/Receipt.tsx` |
| Plain text receipt (no server set) | `receiptText` in `src/screens/Receipt.tsx` |
| Building the snapshot | `buildReceiptDoc` in `src/lib/receiptDoc.ts` (its type, `ReceiptDoc`, is in `receipt-server/src/types.ts`) |
| The address, number and GST | `receiptId`, `receiptNumber`, `receiptUrl`, `gstIncluded` in `src/lib/receiptDoc.ts` |
| Uploading | `uploadReceipt`, `receiptsEnabled`, `ReceiptConfigError` in `src/lib/receiptSync.ts` |
| Sample receipt | `uploadSampleReceipt` in `src/lib/receiptSync.ts` (the **Send test receipt** button) |
| Background steps | `runItem` and `processOutbox` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| Settings ▸ Receipts | `ReceiptSettings` in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| The Worker | `receipt-server/src/index.ts` (routes), `receipt-server/src/validate.ts` (what it accepts), `receipt-server/src/render.ts` (the page and its titles), `receipt-server/src/clientScript.ts` (PDF, image, print) |
| Old sales | `Detail` in `src/screens/Transactions.tsx` (**New receipt**) and the **Receipt** button in `src/screens/Orders.tsx` |

### The snapshot
`buildReceiptDoc` copies everything the page shows, so the Worker needs no Shopify access:
- `receiptId` is the first 20 hex characters of the SHA-256 of `rcpt:` plus the sale's uuid. Nothing is stored or synced for it, so any iPad that has the sale makes the same id. `receiptNumber` is `R-` plus the first eight characters in capitals.
- Totals: `totalCents` is the sale total plus rounding for a sale, and the refund total as it is for a refund (refunds carry no rounding).
- Payments: `payment` builds one row per payment. Cash rounding is added into the row's amount. Card rows keep scheme, masked number, approval code, RRN, a short terminal id, the external reference, time and Zeller's own receipt link. The page shows **Original card receipt** only when that link starts with `https://`.
- GST is `gstIncluded`: one eleventh of the non-gift-card lines when registered, otherwise 0.

### The Worker
`PUT /api/r/<id>` needs `Authorization: Bearer <RECEIPT_SECRET>` (compared in constant time), refuses bodies over 64,000 characters, and runs the body through the validation file, which trims and limits every field and rejects an id that does not match. Anything else is a 4xx. `GET /r/<id>` renders the page with a one-time script nonce, so the page's own PDF script is the only script allowed. The PDF and image are drawn in the customer's browser.

### How failures are handled
`receiptStep` inside `runItem` has three outcomes: success marks the step done; a `ReceiptConfigError` (no URL, no secret, or any non-5xx failure) raises the **Receipt page not published** notification and marks the step done; anything else (a network failure or a 5xx) is held until the end so the item stays queued. `uploadReceipt` throws a `ReceiptConfigError` for a 4xx and a network error for a 5xx.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **QR shows but the page says Receipt not found.** The upload has not landed. Check More ▸ Support & diagnostics ▸ Sync for a queued sale, then the receipt server address and secret.
- **A page has the wrong business name or address.** Something re-uploaded it after the settings changed (see Deep). Fix Settings ▸ Receipts and tap **New receipt** on the sale.
- **A refund receipt shows the wrong title.** The title rule is in `receipt-server/src/render.ts`: it decides from the document's kind and the GST flag.
- **The page shows no order number.** Only the second queue upload adds it. If the Shopify order step is still waiting, so is the number.
- **No Wallet pass button on a gift card sale.** It is hidden while `GIFT_CARD_PASSES` in `src/lib/features.ts` is false.
- **Tests.** `tests/receipt.test.ts` covers the receipt id, GST, the merged lines and card details, cash rounding, refund titles, the Worker's validation and the page's escaping.

pages.title: Split and part payments
pages.summary: Paying one bill in pieces: splitting equally or by an amount, part payments in cash or by gift card, and how the next payment amount is worked out.
pages.lead: One sale can be paid with as many payments as you like, in any mix of card, cash and gift card. The sale finishes by itself when nothing remains.

sections.basic:
### Splitting
On the **Payment** screen tap **Split amount** (**Split the payment** in Simple and Minimal modes). The **Split amount** sheet opens with **First payment** and a keypad.
- **Split equally 2, 3 or 4:** the bill is shared into that many equal payments. Cents that do not divide evenly go to the first payments.
- **Key in an amount and tap Continue:** that is the first payment. It must be less than what remains, otherwise you see *Amount must be less than the remaining total*. **Continue** stays greyed out until the amount is above $0.00.

After you choose, the screen shows **Next payment: $…** and, after a dot, the payments that come after it (**then $…, $…**). Now tap **Card**, **Cash** or **Gift card** and that payment aims for the next payment amount. Tap **Cancel split** to go back to paying the lot.

Example: $100.00 split equally 3 ways is $33.34, then $33.33, then $33.33.

### Each payment counts as one share
With **Split equally**, every payment you take counts as one share, whatever it was and whatever its size. After each one the rest is shared between the people left. Example: $90.00 split 3 ways.
1. The first person pays $30.00 by card. $60.00 remains for 2 people.
2. The second hands over only $20.00 in cash and you take it as a part payment. That counts as their share, so $40.00 remains for 1 person.
3. The last payment is the whole $40.00.

A card that is declined or cancelled takes nothing, so it does not use up a share.

### When the cash does not cover a part of a split
If the customer hands over less than the current payment, the cash screen says how short it is and offers, instead of leaving you to split again:
- **Two payments left:** **Add $… to payment 2** (it shows the old and new amount), or **Go back and change the split**.
- **More than two payments left:** **Add $… to payment 3** (one button for each later payment), or **Spread $… over the other payments** (each later payment rises by the same amount), or **Go back and change the split**.

The cash they did hand over is taken as this payment, and the shortfall moves to the payment you chose. **Spread** only shows when every later payment would go up by a whole number of dollars (for example $30.00 over 3 payments is $10.00 each). If it would not divide into whole dollars the button is left out; choose a payment to add it to instead. **Ask for more** is always an option: just tap more notes and coins.

### Part payments without splitting
You do not have to split first. A payment can simply be less than the bill:
- **Cash:** if the customer hands over less than is due and the bill is not split, tap **Take $… as part payment**. See [[pay/cash]].
- **Cash and card:** if the drawer cannot make the change, the cash screen can offer **Cash $… + the rest another way**.
- **Gift card:** a card with less balance than the bill pays what it has. See [[pay/gift-card]].

In every case the **Payment** screen then says **Remaining**, with *of $…* under it, and the payments so far are listed. Pay the rest any way you like.

### While part of the sale is paid
The cart is locked, so you cannot change items, clear it or save it. **Back** asks **Cancel this sale?**. **Refund & cancel** refunds card payments through the terminal and credits gift-card payments back to the same cards. For cash, the app asks you to collect any exact change previously given and return the exact denominations originally received; it does not optimise this exchange. If a cancellation step fails, the sale stays locked, records electronic returns already completed and offers a safe retry. Do not take another payment for that sale. See [[pay]].

### On the receipt
The receipt lists every payment with its amount, and the sale is sent to Shopify with one payment per entry.
sections.deep:
### How the next payment amount is chosen
The next payment aims for the first of these that applies, never more than what remains:
1. The amount you keyed in on the split sheet.
2. An equal share, when **Split equally** is active and more than one share is left.
3. Everything that remains.

A keyed amount only applies to the **next** payment. Once it is paid, the screen goes back to aiming for everything that remains, unless you split again. Example: $100.00 with $30.00 keyed. After the $30.00 is paid, $70.00 remains and the next payment aims for $70.00, not $30.00.

### Equal shares and cents
The shares are worked out from what **remains**, so they are re-worked after every payment. Spare cents go to the earliest shares, which is why the first payer can be one cent more. The shares always add up exactly to what remains.

### Rounding in a split
Cash rounding only applies to the payment that clears the whole of what remains. Earlier shares are always exact, and so are card payments. See [[pay/cash]].

### Each payment is its own record
Every payment keeps its own method, amount, and for cards its own fee. The Shopify order gets one payment per entry, named **Zeller**, **Cash** or **Gift card**.

### Cancelling
**Refund & cancel** refunds each card payment through the terminal and credits each gift-card tender back to its original Shopify card. A unique transaction note and per-tender progress prevent a retry from crediting the same card twice. After electronic returns finish, the cashier collects any change previously given and returns the original cash tender using the exact saved denominations (or enters a manual denomination count for older tenders). If any step fails, payment methods are disabled and the cancellation can be retried.
sections.advanced:
### Working out the next payment
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Pay.tsx: plan is the list of payments still to take] --> B{more than one part}
  B -->|yes| C[target is the first part]
  B -->|no| D[target is what remains]
  C --> E[cap at remaining]
  D --> E
  E --> F[card cash or gift card aims for this amount]
  F --> G{cash short on this part}
  G -->|yes| H[shortChoices: add to a later part, spread, or change the split]
  G -->|no| I[addTender uses up the first part]
  H --> I
  I --> J[planAfter shares what is left over the later parts]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The next payment amount (`target`) and the `plan` state | `Pay` in `src/screens/Pay.tsx` |
| The split plan and the shortfall choices | `equalPlan`, `firstPlan`, `planTarget`, `planAfter`, `shortChoices`, `applyShortChoice` in `src/lib/splitPlan.ts` |
| The shortfall buttons | `CashSheet` in `src/screens/CashSheet.tsx` |
| Adding a payment | `addTender` in `src/screens/Pay.tsx` |
| Sharing cents | `allocate` in `src/lib/money.ts` (largest remainder) |
| What has been paid | `paidTotal` in `src/lib/saleBuilder.ts` |
| Cancelling a part-paid sale | `abandon` in `src/screens/Pay.tsx` |
| The keypad on the split sheet | `Keypad` in `src/ui/kit.tsx` |

`plan` is a list of cents, one per payment still to take. **Split equally n** makes it from `allocate`; a keyed first amount makes `[amount, rest]`. `target` is the smaller of what remains and the first part, or what remains when the plan has one part or none. `addTender` uses up the first part on any payment of any size, then either takes the plan the cash screen chose (see `shortChoices`) or shares what is left over the later parts with `planAfter`. The plan lives only in the `Pay` screen's state, so it is not saved. The payments themselves are saved on the cart as `cart.tenders`.

`Keypad` greys out **Continue** for $0.00, and the split sheet refuses an amount at or above what remains, so a split can never be zero or the whole bill.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **Next payment shows the wrong amount.** A payment was added since you split (it uses up the first part), or the later parts were re-worked from a smaller remainder or moved by a shortfall choice.
- **Cancel split is missing.** It only shows while `plan` has more than one part. With one share left the screen is simply aiming for what remains.
- **The split is gone after reopening the app.** Expected: it is screen state. The payments already taken are still on the cart.
- **Tests.** The sharing maths is covered in `tests/lib.test.ts` (`allocate`). The plan rules are in `tests/splitplan.test.ts`. Cash and sale building are in `tests/cashsale.test.ts` and `tests/sale.test.ts`.

pages.title: Checkout: the main screen
pages.summary: Adding items to a sale: the Quick Menu grid, All products, the keypad, search, scanning, and the cart.
pages.lead: Checkout is where every sale starts. You add things to the cart here, then press **Charge** to take payment.

sections.basic:
### The three ways to add items
At the top of the left side, pick one:
- **Quick Menu**: your grid of tiles (items, categories, discounts and action buttons). This is the fastest way for the things you sell most.
- **All products**: every product in alphabetical order, with a filter box. Use it for anything that is not on the grid.
- **Keypad**: key in an amount and press **Add** for something with no item. It goes in the cart as a "Custom amount".

On the Quick Menu, a tile that opens a **category** takes you into it. The bar above the tiles shows where you are (for example *Home > Dragons > Highland cow*). Tap any earlier name to jump back there, or tap the arrow to go back one step.

### Items with several variations
If a product has more than one variation (a colour or size), tapping it replaces the grid with one tile per variation. Tap the one you want and it is added, then you are back where you were. Out-of-stock variations can still be sold: the stock count is allowed to go below zero, and the screen warns you with "stock will go negative".

### Adding more than one
Tap the item again for each one (the same item joins the same cart line), or change the number on its line in the cart with **−** and **+**. There is no quantity picker on the grid.

### Other ways to find things
- **Search** (the bar at the top): finds items (by name, variation, SKU or barcode), customers, discounts and saved carts. Tap a result to use it.
- **Scan**: a Bluetooth scanner works whenever you are on Checkout and no pop-up is open. The camera icon scans with the iPad's camera. A scanned item is added straight away.
- Scanning a **cashier pass** signs that person in (your cart stays as it is). Scanning a **gift card QR** here tells you to redeem it from Charge ▸ Gift card.

### The cart
On an iPad the cart is always on the right. On a phone, a bar at the bottom shows the item count and total; tap it to open the cart. Press **Charge** when you are ready; if an item in the cart has a customer warning, you read it first (see [[sales/cart-warnings]]). Details are on [[sales/cart-and-prices|The cart and how prices are worked out]].

### The bar along the top
The bar along the very top of the screen is there on every screen except the Sign in screen. It shows the time, the shop logo and name, this register's name, the reader chip, the sync chip and the battery. On an iPad the chips always show **Reader ready** and **Synced** when all is well. If something is wrong you get an amber or red chip instead (\"Reader issue\", \"Offline · 2 queued\", \"Sync issue\"). Tap it to go to the page that explains it. On a phone the reader chip only appears when there is a problem. The bar stays at the top while the screensaver is showing; it does not respond to touches then.

### When you cannot change the cart
Once part of a sale has been paid, the cart is locked and you see "Payment in progress". Finish the payment or cancel it first.
sections.deep:
### Why a tap does different things
A tile is one of several kinds: an item, a category, a display group, a discount, or an action (such as Custom amount, Lock POS, Price check, Stock check or Check change). Items and variations go into the cart; categories and groups open a level of the grid; discounts apply to the whole cart; actions open a sheet or do a job. Categories can contain categories to any depth.

### What "consolidate" means
By default, adding the same item again raises the quantity on its existing line instead of making a second line. A line is **not** merged into if it has been changed in some way (its price adjusted, a discount put on it, or a note added), because merging would mix a special line with a normal one. This can be turned off in Settings (Checkout ▸ Consolidate identical items).

### How scanning finds an item
A barcode is compared after removing spaces and leading zeros, so a 12-digit UPC and a 13-digit EAN with a leading 0 match the same item. If no barcode matches, the scan is tried as an exact SKU. If nothing matches you see "No item for …".

### Why the grid sometimes does not show an item you expect
An item that sits in both a sub-category and its parent category shows only in the sub-category. Items you pin yourself as tiles are never hidden by that rule.

### Your cart is saved as you go
Every change to the cart is written to the device (after a very short delay), so closing the app does not lose it.
sections.advanced:
### What happens on a tap
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  T[Tap an item tile or row] --> A[addItems in Checkout.tsx]
  A -->|one variant| B[add]
  A -->|several variants| P[VariantPicker sub-page]
  P -->|tap one| B
  B --> L{cart locked? tenders present}
  L -->|yes| X[alert: Payment in progress]
  L -->|no| C[ops.addVariant: cartOps.ts]
  C --> S[useApp setCart: store.ts]
  S --> W[persist 'pos' to storage, 400 ms debounce]
  S --> R[usePriced: selectors.ts]
  R --> Q[priceCart: pricing.ts]
  Q --> V[CartPane re-renders with the new totals]
```

### What happens on a scan
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  H[HidScanner or CameraScanner] --> O[onScan in Checkout.tsx]
  O --> B{isBadgeCode?}
  B -->|yes| I[signInWithPass, cart unchanged]
  B -->|no| F[ops.findByBarcode: barcode, then SKU]
  F -->|found| A[add 1 of the variant]
  F -->|not found| G{isGiftQr?}
  G -->|yes| M[toast: redeem from Charge, Gift card]
  G -->|no| N[toast: No item for code]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The screen, tabs, search, scanning | `src/screens/Checkout.tsx` (`Checkout`) |
| The bar along the top (clock, shop, reader and sync chips, battery) | `src/ui/AppStatusBar.tsx` |
| Cart edits (pure) | `src/lib/cartOps.ts`: `addVariant`, `setQty`, `removeLine`, `patchLine`, `swapVariant`, `findByBarcode`, `normaliseBarcode` |
| The line-merge rule | `sameLine` in `cartOps.ts` (item, same variant, no override, no discount, no note) |
| Grid path and the variation sub-page | `src/lib/gridNav.ts`, `VariantPicker` in `src/screens/Tiles.tsx`, rules in `src/lib/lookup.ts` |
| Store and saving | `src/state/store.ts` (`setCart`, `persist`) |
| Scanner focus rules | `HidScanner` in `src/screens/Scanner.tsx`, `src/lib/focusGuard.ts` |

### Reading the code for a fault
- **A scan adds nothing and says "No item"**: the variant's `barcode` and `sku` on this device do not match what was scanned. A missing barcode on the item in Shopify is the usual cause; fix it there, then import again in Settings ▸ Shopify.
- **A tap does nothing and shows "Payment in progress"**: `cart.tenders` has an entry, so `locked` is true. Finish or cancel the payment. A part-paid sale left over from a crash is the usual reason.
- **The scanner stops working**: `HidScanner` is enabled only when `active`, the tab is Checkout, no sheet is open, no camera is open and the navigation stack is empty. Any one of those being false disables it.
- **An item is on the grid but missing inside a category**: see `ownProductIds` in `src/lib/gridNav.ts` (deepest sub-category wins).

pages.title: Bundle deals and the builder
pages.summary: Set up "buy these together, pay less" deals in Settings, and how they show up in the cart and at payment.
pages.lead: A bundle deal changes the price when a customer buys certain items together, for example *2 Highland Cows for $2 off*. You build them in Settings, and the cart applies them by itself.

sections.basic:
### Who can make them, and where
Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Discounts & bundles**. Managers and owners can open Settings. When staff accounts and the PIN requirement are in use, a signed-in cashier cannot, so they only ever see the deals working in the cart. With no accounts set up, the till acts as the owner and anyone can. See [[staff]] for how staff roles work.

The list shows every deal with its name, whether it is **Live**, **Scheduled**, **Ended** or **Off**, and a one-line summary such as *2 × Highland Cow → $2.00 off*. The switch on the right turns a deal on or off without deleting it. Tap a row to change it.

### Making a deal
Tap **New bundle deal**, then work down the screen:
1. **Deal name**: this is what the customer sees on the cart and receipt. Use something short, like *Cow pair*.
2. **What the customer buys**: each **Group** is "this many items from this list".
   - Tap **Pick items** and search. Tapping a product includes **every variation** of it. To be stricter, tap the options icon beside a product that has several variations and tick only the ones you want.
   - Use the **−** and **+** to set how many from the group are needed (it shows as *2 ×*).
   - **Add another group of items** if the deal mixes different things, such as one dragon and one egg.
3. **The deal**: choose **$ off**, **% off** or **Set price**, then type the amount.
   - **$ off**: takes that many dollars off the items together.
   - **% off**: takes that percentage off the items.
   - **Set price**: the items together cost exactly that amount.
4. **Take it off** appears when the deal has more than one item. **Spread over all items** shares the saving across everything in the deal. **Only group 1** (or 2, 3 …) takes the whole saving from that group's items only.
5. **Limits** (all optional): **Most times per order**, and **Starts** and **Ends** dates written like `2026-12-24`. The end date counts the whole day.
6. **Recommended pairs** (optional, see below).
7. Tap **Create deal**. The **Summary** box at the bottom shows what you have built before you save.

If something is missing, red notes appear under the form when you tap **Create deal** and say what (for example *Give the deal a name.* or *Group 1 has no items. Pick at least one.*). **Delete deal** asks first, and the deal stops applying straight away.

### Recommended pairs
Some deals only make sense for certain combinations, like matching colours. Under **Recommended pairs** tap **Add a recommended pair** and choose one variation for each item in the deal.

Every variation still gets the deal. A recommended pair guides the matcher and cashier:
- If the cashier rings up a different combination, they are asked to check it before payment (see below).
- When more than one eligible combination is available, the POS prefers the recommended combination, even if another combination would produce a larger saving.

For many variations, tap **Auto** next to **Add a recommended pair**. It pairs variations that have the same style and the same colour in each item of the deal, for example a Gemstone egg in *Crushed Blue* with the Mini Gemstone dragon in *Crushed Blue*. A Gemstone item never pairs with a Rose one. Colours are compared as a whole, so *Green* never pairs with *Green Black Dual Colour*, but *Black/Red*, *Black & Red* and *Red Black* count as the same colours. Words like *Dual Colour*, *Assorted* and a tag in brackets such as *(EOP)* are only ignored when nothing closer is left to match. Each variation is used once, and variations with no partner are skipped. A note under the buttons says how many pairs were added and lists the variations that found no match. Auto adds to the pairs you already have and never changes them. If the items in the deal have no style in common (like *Highland Cow* and *Tadling*), only the colours are compared. Check the list afterwards, since Auto reads names only.

For many variations, **Export variation JSON** shares each deal position's allowed variant IDs and names. Ask an LLM to fill the `recommended` array with one variant ID per position, then paste its JSON response into **Import pairs JSON**. The app checks every ID against the variations allowed in that position before replacing the current pairs.

If you change the items or quantities after adding pairs, you are asked **Clear recommended pairs?**, because the old pairs no longer fit.

### In the cart
When items qualify, a **Bundle deals** block appears under the lines with one card per deal. Each card names the deal, the saving, and every item and variation in it. A green tick says **Recommended pair**. An amber warning says **Not a recommended pair**.

The deal also appears as its own row under each line it discounted, showing the deal's name and the amount.

### The check before payment
If any deal in the cart is **Not a recommended pair**, tapping **Charge** first opens **Check these bundles**. The customer still gets the deal. Look at the items and ask whether it is what they want, then tap **Continue to payment**, or **Edit cart** to change something. You are only asked again if the combination changes. In the guided checkout the same warning appears on the **Check** step, headed *Check these deals with the customer*.

If the sale also has price adjustments, those are reviewed first, then the bundle check.

### Good to know
- A single item unit can only be in **one** deal. If two deals could use the same unit, the POS gives the customer the bigger saving.
- A line that gets a bundle discount does not also get its own line discount.
- Items tagged `no-discount`, gift cards and custom amounts never count towards a deal.
- A deal needs enough units. A group of 3 needs 3 of those items in the cart.
- **Price check** (see [[sales/lookup-tiles]]) lists the bundle deals an item can be part of. That is only a hint: it cannot know what else is in the cart.
- Changes you save are shared with the other registers. They get them within about 25 seconds while the app is open.
sections.deep:
### How the POS chooses between deals
Several deals can apply to one order, and a unit can only be used once. When the cart could be matched more than one way, the POS tries the possible ways and prefers, in order:
1. more recommended pairs,
2. the biggest total saving,
3. fewer deal applications (so a bigger lot beats two smaller ones),
4. the deal with the lower priority number,
5. the deal that comes first in the list.

This means a recommended variation pairing can be chosen over a different pairing with a larger discount. Without any available recommended pairs, savings remain the primary choice.

### Worked examples
- *2 Highland Cows for $2 off*, customer buys 3 cows: one application ($2 off two cows). The third cow is at full price.
- *Dragon + Egg, set price $12*, customer buys a dragon ($9) and an egg ($4): together $13, so the deal takes $1 off. If they already cost less than the set price, the deal does nothing. A deal never raises a price.
- *% off pair, 10%*, with **Only group 2**: the 10% is worked out on, and taken off, group 2's items only.
- A cashier changed a unit's price for the sale. Deals use the changed price, and never take a price below $0.

### How the saving is shared between items
For **Spread over all items** the saving is divided between the units in proportion to their prices. For **Only group N** only that group's units take it, and never more than they cost.

### Dates
The Starts date is the first moment of that day and the Ends date is the last moment of that day, both by the iPad's own clock and time zone. A deal is live when it is switched on and inside its dates. A wrong date or time on a register changes which deals it applies.

### Sharing between registers
Deals are kept with the other shared settings (staff, fees, cash rounding, the PIN requirement and price adjustment limits). Saving a deal sends the whole set. If the upload fails, this register keeps the change pending and retries while the app is open, about every 25 seconds. Other registers receive it on a later poll after the upload succeeds. Check **Support & diagnostics ▸ Sync** if the shared-settings upload reports an error.

### Where deals sit in the price
Bundles are worked out first, before Shopify automatic discounts, a line's own discount, the cart discount and any price adjustments. Units used by a bundle are not used by an automatic discount. See [[sales/cart-and-prices]] for the full order.
sections.advanced:
### From the editor to a discounted cart
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[DealEditor in BundleBuilder.tsx] --> B[upsertDeal in bundleForm.ts: groups become sets]
  B --> C[stringifyBundleConfig then patchSettings bundlesJson]
  C --> D[pushSharedSettings in sync.ts]
  D -->|sent| E[other registers: pullSettings inside pollShared every 25 s]
  D -->|offline or error| F[keep change pending and retry on foreground poll]
  C --> G[usePriced in selectors.ts re-prices the cart]
  G --> H[priceCart step 1 calls matchBundles]
```

### How a match is found
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[priceCart in pricing.ts: item lines that are discountable] --> B[matchBundles in bundles.ts]
  B --> C[drop deals that are off or outside their dates: dealLive]
  C --> D[list every way each deal can be filled from the cart]
  D --> E[greedy pass: biggest saving first]
  E --> F[search for a better combination up to 20000 steps]
  F --> G{better total saving?}
  G -->|yes| H[keep it]
  G -->|equal| I[prefer more recommended pairs then fewer applications]
  H --> J[AppliedBundle cards and one discount row per line per deal]
  I --> J
```
The greedy pass always gives a valid answer first. If the search hits its step limit it keeps the best result found so far, so a very large cart can get a good answer that is not guaranteed to be the best.

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Auto pairing: styles, colours, tiers, leftovers | `autoRecommendedPairs` in `src/lib/autoPairs.ts`; the **Auto** button (`runAuto`) in `DealEditor` |
| The list, editor, item picker, pair picker, JSON view | `BundlesEditor`, `DealEditor`, `ItemPicker`, `PairPicker`, `JsonEditor` in `src/screens/BundleBuilder.tsx` (Settings ▸ Discounts & bundles is drawn by `Settings.tsx`) |
| Form to deal and back, ids, dates, save checks | `formToDeal`, `dealToForm`, `upsertDeal`, `removeDeal`, `pruneSets`, `makeDealId`, `formProblems`, `dealWindow` in `src/lib/bundleForm.ts` |
| Reading and checking the saved JSON | `parseBundleConfig`, `validateBundleConfig` in `src/lib/bundles.ts` |
| Matching | `matchBundles`, `dealLive`, `bundleStatus` in `src/lib/bundles.ts` |
| Pricing step | step 1 of `priceCart` in `src/lib/pricing.ts` |
| Reading the setting | `bundleConfig` in `src/lib/sync.ts`; `usePriced` in `src/state/selectors.ts` |
| Check before payment | `needsBundleCheck`, `bundleReviewKey`, `oddBundles` in `src/lib/bundles.ts`; the **Check these bundles** sheet in `CartPane.tsx`; the **Check** step in `GuidedCheckout.tsx` |
| The card in the cart | `BundleRow` in `src/screens/CartPane.tsx` |
| Exchanges | `Refund.tsx` prices the replacement items with `bundleConfig` too |

### How a deal is stored
The setting is `settings.bundlesJson`, a JSON text of `{ version, items, discounts }`. `items` is a map of **set id to a list of product or variation ids**. Each deal's `sets` lists set ids, once per unit needed, so *2 cows* is `["x", "x"]`.

The builder saves each group as a set named `<dealId>_1`, `<dealId>_2` and so on, and repeats a set for its quantity. A new deal's id comes from its name (`makeDealId` makes it unique, for example `cow_pair_2`). Editing keeps the id even if the name changes. `pruneSets` removes sets that no deal uses.

The three modes are stored as `mode` `delta` (`price_delta_cents` negative), `fixed_price` (`price_delta_cents` is the price) and `percent` (`percent`). `apply_to` names the set the saving comes from. `recommended` is a list of variation id lists, one id per unit.

A product id in a set matches all of its variations. A variation id matches only that one. The JSON view (**Advanced: edit as JSON**) edits the same text, and saving it rewrites the deals in the list.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **No deal applies at all.** `bundleConfig` returns null when the saved text cannot be read, and pricing then skips bundles with no message. Open Settings ▸ Discounts & bundles: if the text is unreadable the editor opens on the JSON view and says why.
- **One deal does not apply.** Work through it in this order: is it **Live** (switched on, inside its dates by this iPad's clock)? Is the item or its product in the group, and is it still in the catalogue (the editor warns about items that are no longer synced)? Does the cart hold enough units for every group? Is the item tagged `no-discount`, or a gift card or custom amount? Has **Most times per order** been reached? Does the deal save anything (a **Set price** at or above what the items cost saves $0, so it is skipped)? Did another deal win with a bigger saving?
- **The saving is on the wrong item.** Check **Take it off** (`apply_to`).
- **A change did not reach another register.** Look at the **Sync** strip and wait one 25 second tick. If the saving register was offline, there was no retry (see Sharing).
- **A line discount you set disappeared.** The line also got a bundle discount, which blocks the manual one (see [[sales/cart-and-prices]]).
- **Tests.** `tests/autopairs.test.ts` covers Auto pairing. `tests/bundleform.test.ts` covers percent and dated deals, recommended pairs, the form round trip, the checkout check, and a deal built in the GUI running through `priceCart`. `tests/lib.test.ts` covers a price override feeding a bundle.

pages.title: The cart and how prices are worked out
pages.summary: What is in the cart, how to change a line, and how bundles, automatic deals and discounts turn into the final price.
pages.lead: The cart is the list of what the customer is buying. The total at the bottom is always the final price after every deal.

sections.basic:
### Reading a line
Each line shows the item and variation, then **quantity × price** (for example *13 × $4.00*). If a discount applies, the full price is struck through with the final price beside it, and each discount sits on its own green row underneath with the amount taken off. A deal that applied more than once shows **(x2)** after its name.

### Changing a line
- **Swipe left** on a line to remove it (let go past halfway and tap the red button, or swipe all the way across).
- **Tap** a line to edit it:
  - **− / +** change the quantity (going to 0 removes the line).
  - **Variation** chips swap to another variation of the same product.
  - **Discount** puts a percentage or dollar discount on this line only.
  - **Item price adjustment** sets a new unit price for this sale. Choose **Fixed quantity** for a set number of units, or **All in cart** for every unit of this variant, including ones added later. **Reset to catalogue price** undoes it.
  - **Line price adjustment** sets what the whole line costs after its deals and discounts. It cannot raise the line price.
  - **Note** adds a note to the line.
  - **Remove item** takes it out.

### The customer
Tap the person row at the top of the cart to add a customer to the sale, or the small ✕ to take them off. You can create a new customer from the ••• menu.

### The ••• menu
**Clear cart**, **Save cart** (for later; see saved carts), **Create customer**, **Custom amount**, **Apply cart discount**, **Whole order price**, **Sell gift card**, **Check gift card**, and **Check change** (can we make change for this cart?).

### Bundle deals
When items in the cart qualify for a bundle deal, a **Bundle deals** block appears under the lines with one card per deal, naming each item and variation and the saving. A card may say **Recommended pair** or **Not a recommended pair**. The customer gets the deal either way. When you press **Charge** with a "not a recommended pair" bundle in the cart, a sheet shows it once so you can check it is what the customer wants (**Edit cart** or **Continue to payment**).

### What cannot be discounted
Gift cards, custom amounts, and any item tagged `no-discount` in Shopify. Their line shows "Not discountable" in the editor.

### The total
Above the **Charge** button you see **Items** (the full price), each deal in green with its saving, and the final amount on the button. The count underneath is the total number of items.

```screen
title: Cart
sub: 3 items
label: Items
row: Highland Cow · Cream ×1 | $12.50
row: Gemstone egg · Crushed Blue ×2 | $18.00
label: Total
row: Items | $30.50
row: Cow pair | −$2.00
primary: !1 Charge  $28.50
note: The green line is a bundle deal, and the price on the button is what the customer pays.
```

### Price adjustments and review
- **Whole order price** sets a lower total for the order. The saving is shared across eligible items; gift cards are never reduced. A whole order price and line price adjustments cannot be used together.
- Add a **Reason (optional)** when setting an item, line or whole order price if you want to explain it.
- Before payment, **Check the price adjustments** shows manual price changes. Resolve every flagged row with **Keep**, **Adjust** or **Remove** before continuing. If your role cannot keep or change it, remove it or ask a manager or owner.
- If quantity, discounts or prices change after an adjustment was set, the affected adjustment is flagged for another look.

See [[concepts/roles]] for role limits and [[concepts/money]] for cents and rounding.
sections.deep:
### The order discounts are applied in
The price is built in four steps, always in this order:
1. **Bundle deals** (the deals you set up in Settings ▸ Discounts & bundles).
2. **Automatic discounts** imported from Shopify.
3. **The line's own discount** (the one you set in the line editor).
4. **The cart discount.**

Each step works on what is left after the one before it, and a discount never takes a line below $0.

### Rules that follow from that
- A single unit can be part of **one** bundle deal or **one** automatic discount, never two. Several different deals can apply in the same order, and the POS picks the combination with the biggest total saving for the customer.
- A line that received a bundle discount does **not** also get its own line discount.
- The cart discount is spread over the remaining value of every line that can be discounted, in proportion to that value. The pieces add up exactly: no cent is lost or invented.
- A percentage is rounded to the nearest cent (half up).
- The POS works out Shopify's automatic discounts itself, so the total on screen is instant and works offline. Shopify's own "combines with" settings are not read.

### A worked example
A customer buys 2 Highland cows and 8 Tadlings. The shop has an automatic deal for 2 cows ($2 off), one for 3 Tadlings ($5 off) and one for 5 Tadlings ($10 off). The cows get the $2 deal. Of the 8 Tadlings, 5 take the $10 deal and the other 3 take the $5 deal, so the Tadling line shows two discount rows, **5x Tadlings** (−$10) and **3x Tadlings** (−$5). (The prices here are only to show the shape.)

### Price adjustment versus discount
There are three separate adjustments:
- **Item price** changes a unit price before bundle, automatic and manual discounts. **Fixed quantity** stores how many units were priced; if that count changes later it is flagged. **All in cart** follows every unit of that variant in this order, including later additions. Gift cards cannot have an item price adjustment.
- **Line price** sets the final cost of the whole line after its bundle, automatic and line discounts. It never raises the price, and a cart discount skips that line.
- **Whole order price** sets the order's final total and spreads its saving over eligible lines in proportion to their remaining value. It cannot raise the total, go below the gift-card value, or be active at the same time as line price adjustments. Setting one asks before removing the other.

An item price adjustment is part of the unit price used by discounts. Line and whole-order prices are kept as separate adjustment rows. Reasons are optional; when supplied, they are kept with the sale, included in the Shopify order's `pos_adjustments` attribute and grouped in Reports.

### When review is needed
Charge opens **Check the price adjustments** before payment the first time there are manual price changes, and again when an adjustment or something it depends on changes. Rows needing a second look appear first. Examples include changing a line's quantity, changing a fixed-quantity item's count, changing a line's price or discounts, or changing the whole order's items, prices or discounts. **Keep** confirms the same price against the current cart; **Adjust** edits it; **Remove** restores the normal price. A flagged row must be resolved to continue.

A cashier or manager may be prevented from setting, keeping or changing particular price-adjustment types. Removing an adjustment is always available. Owners cannot be restricted from setting them.

### Prices sent to Shopify
Shopify needs a whole-cent price per unit. When a line's final price does not divide evenly, the POS splits it into at most two groups of units that differ by one cent, so the pieces add up to the line total exactly. For example, $10.00 for 3 units becomes 2 units at $3.33 and 1 unit at $3.34.
sections.advanced:
### The pricing pipeline
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  U[usePriced: src/state/selectors.ts] --> P[priceCart cart, ctx]
  P --> W[Work per line: item price or catalogue unit price]
  W --> B1[1 matchBundles: bundles.ts]
  B1 --> B2[2 chooseAutoDiscounts: pricing.ts]
  B2 --> B3[3 manual line discount]
  B3 --> B4[4 cart discount except fixed line prices]
  B4 --> B5[5 apply line price adjustments]
  B5 --> B6[6 spread whole order price over eligible lines]
  B6 --> R[PricedCart totals and adjustment rows]
  R --> UI[CartPane, Pay, receipts]
  R --> S[splitLineForOrder for Shopify order lines]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The whole pipeline | `priceCart` in `src/lib/pricing.ts` |
| Running it live | `usePriced` in `src/state/selectors.ts` (re-runs when the cart, catalogue, automatic discounts or the bundles setting change) |
| Bundle matching | `matchBundles` in `src/lib/bundles.ts` |
| Automatic discounts | `chooseAutoDiscounts`, `autoMove`, `isLot`, `activeNow` in `src/lib/pricing.ts` |
| Clamping a discount to what is left | the local `add` in `priceCart` (`Math.min(d.cents, remaining(w))`) and `remaining` |
| Percent and spreading cents | `pctOf`, `allocate` in `src/lib/money.ts` |
| Which lines are discountable | `discountable` in `priceCart`: not `gift_card`, not `noDiscount`, no `no-discount` tag (`NO_DISCOUNT_TAG`) |
| Rows shown in the cart | `invoiceRows`, `unitLine` in `src/lib/invoiceRows.ts` |
| The cart screen | `src/screens/CartPane.tsx`; the line editor `LineEditor` in `src/screens/sheets.tsx` |
| Item, line and whole-order price rules | `setItemPrice` in `src/lib/cartOps.ts`; `makeAdjust`, `reviewReasons` in `src/lib/lineAdjust.ts`; `orderAdjustProblem`, `orderReviewReasons` in `src/lib/orderAdjust.ts` |
| Adjustment rows and payment gate | `adjustmentRows`, `needsAdjustReview`, `unresolvedRows` in `src/lib/adjustReview.ts`; `AdjustmentReviewSheet` in `src/screens/AdjustmentReview.tsx` |
| Price-adjustment role rules | `src/lib/adjustPerms.ts`, `AdjustRoleRules` in `src/screens/Staff.tsx` |
| Saving reasons to sales and reports | `saleAdjustments` in `src/lib/adjustReview.ts`, `encodeAdjustments` in `src/lib/adjustReason.ts`, `applyRecord` in `src/lib/rollup.ts` |
| Splitting for Shopify | `splitLineForOrder` in `src/lib/pricing.ts` |
| Tests | `tests/itemadjust.test.ts`, `tests/lineadjust.test.ts`, `tests/orderadjust.test.ts`, `tests/adjustreview.test.ts`, `tests/adjustreason.test.ts`, `tests/adjustperms.test.ts`; plus `tests/compound.test.ts`, `tests/autocombine.test.ts`, `tests/bundleform.test.ts`, `tests/swipe.test.ts` |

### The data it returns
