`PricedCart` has `lines` (each with `baseUnitCents`, `grossCents`, `discounts`, `discountCents`, `netCents`, `bundleUnits`), the cart totals `itemsCents`, `discountCents` and `netCents`, `deals` (the discounts rolled up by type and label, which is what the totals area lists), and `bundles` (one entry per bundle application, with the units it used). Each entry in `discounts` has a `type` (`bundle`, `auto`, `manual` or `cart`), a `label`, `cents`, and for repeated deals a `times` count.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **A deal you expect did not apply.** Check, in order: is the line discountable (tag, `noDiscount`, gift card or custom amount)? Is the discount inside its dates (`activeNow` compares `startsAt` and `endsAt`)? Does the line's product, variation or collection match the discount's target (`matches`)? For a bundle, check its on/off switch, dates and "most times per order" in the bundle editor.
- **A line discount you set vanished from the receipt.** The line also got a bundle discount, and step 3 skips lines that did (`w.discounts.some(d => d.type === 'bundle')`).
- **The total is a cent out against Shopify.** Compare `splitLineForOrder` output with the order lines; the groups must add to `netCents`.
- **A discount seems to apply to the wrong line.** The cart discount is spread over every discountable line, so each gets a share; look at the per-line `discounts` array, not just the rolled-up `deals`.
- **Debugging a cart.** Call `priceCart` from a test with the same cart and context as the sale (see `tests/autocombine.test.ts` for how a context is built).

pages.title: Customer warnings at Charge
pages.summary: Prompts that appear before payment when the cart holds a chosen item or category, such as "joints are fragile", and how to set them up.
pages.lead: A customer warning is a message the till shows the cashier when they press **Charge**, before payment starts. Use it for things the customer should be told, for example *Joints are fragile, do not bend or apply pressure as it will snap* on a mini dragon.

sections.basic:
### What the cashier sees
Tap **Charge**. If anything in the cart has a warning, a popup opens before the price adjustments and bundle checks. The popup is the warning: its title is the header that was set (*Customer Warning* if left blank), with a warning icon, and the message is the big text in the middle. **For:** under the message names the items that set it off.

```screen
title: Customer Warning
text: Fragile. Do not bend, drop or apply pressure to the item.
label: For
text: Mini dragon · Grey
button: Back to cart
primary: !1 I have read this and dealt with it
note: The cashier must tick to continue if the warning asks for it.
```
- With one warning there is just the message, **Continue to payment** and **Back to cart**.
- With several warnings it is still one popup, one warning per page. Dots at the bottom show which page you are on. Tap **Next** and **Back** to move between them.
- On the last warning, **Next** becomes **Continue to payment**. **Back to cart** is on every page and closes the popup so you can change the cart.
- If a warning needs ticking, tap **I have read this and dealt with it** on each one. **Continue to payment** stays off until every warning that needs it has been ticked, and a note says how many are left.

Once you have carried on from a warning, it is not asked again on the same sale unless it changes (its text is edited, or another line sets it off). A warning set to always show comes up every time you press Charge.

### Setting them up
Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Cart warnings** (managers and owners). Tap **Add warning**, then:
1. **Header**: the title of the window. Leave it blank for *Customer Warning*.
2. **Message for the cashier**: the text shown.
3. **Show on every sale**: turn on to show it on every Charge, whatever is in the cart.
4. **Cashier must tick it**: turn on to stop payment until the cashier ticks that they have read it and dealt with it.
5. **Shows when the cart has**: pick **Variation**, **Product** or **Category**, search, and tap the one you want. A *Product* covers every variation of it. A *Category* is a Shopify collection, so it covers every product in it. This is hidden when **Show on every sale** is on.
6. Tap **Save**. **Save** stays off until there is a message and something to attach it to (or Show on every sale is on).

In the list, **On** and **Off** switch a warning without deleting it. **Edit** and **Delete** are on each card. Delete asks first.

### Good to know
- Gift cards and custom amounts never set a warning off.
- Warnings are shared with the other registers, like the staff list and bundle deals.
- Practice runs in Training never show the shop's real warnings.
- A warning for an item or category that has since been removed from the catalogue shows its name as *no longer in the catalogue*. It never fires. Edit it or delete it.
sections.deep:
### Order of the checks
Charge runs the checks in this order, and each one only appears if it applies: customer warnings, then **Check the price adjustments**, then **Check these bundles**, then the Payment screen. A sale that is already part paid goes straight to Payment and skips all three.

### What counts as "already seen"
When you tap **Continue to payment**, the till remembers each warning you carried on from, along with which cart lines set it off and the exact header and message. If you come back to the cart and press Charge again, only warnings that are new or changed appear. Warnings set to always show are never remembered. Starting a new sale (an empty cart) forgets everything.

### Ticking
Ticking is per warning, and it resets each time the window opens, so a cashier cannot tick on one visit and skip on the next. Ticking again un-ticks. **Next** and **Back** are always free, and **Continue to payment** only takes the place of **Next** on the last warning so every one is paged through.

### Order of the warnings
Warnings appear in the order they were added in Settings.
sections.advanced:
### From Charge to payment
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Charge in CartPane.tsx or takePayment in GuidedCheckout.tsx] --> B{sale part paid}
  B -->|yes| P[adjustment review check]
  B -->|no| C[useCartWarningGate pages]
  C -->|none| P
  C -->|some| D[CartWarningsSheet]
  D -->|Continue| E[markSeen then afterWarnings]
  E --> P
  P --> F[bundle check then pay screen]
```

### Where it lives
- `src/lib/cartWarnings.ts`: `matchCartWarnings` finds which warnings the cart sets off (variant, product, or collection through `collectionsOfProduct`; `category` is read as `collection`), `warningKey` fingerprints one, `pendingCartWarnings` drops those already seen, `unacknowledged` lists those still to tick.
- `src/screens/CartWarningsSheet.tsx`: the popup, and `useCartWarningGate`, the hook both checkouts use. It is a `Sheet` in popup mode (`src/ui/kit.tsx`), with the dots from `PageDots`, the same ones the Show stage uses.
- `src/screens/CartWarningsSettings.tsx`: the editor under Settings ▸ Cart warnings.
- `Settings.cartWarnings` in `src/state/store.ts`, typed by `CartWarning` in `src/lib/types.ts`.
- Shared between registers by `pushSharedSettings` and `pullSettings` in `src/lib/sync.ts`.
- `sandboxSettings` in `src/lib/trainingSandbox.ts` sets `cartWarnings: []` so practice never meets the real ones.
- Popup controls (Back, Next, the tick, Continue to payment, Back to cart) are the `warning.*` spots in `src/lib/trainingSpots.ts`, placed on `sheet_cart_warnings` in `src/lib/appControls.ts` and `src/app.navgraph`.

### Tracing a warning that does not show
1. Is it **On** in Settings ▸ Cart warnings, and does it have a message and a target (or Show on every sale)?
2. Does the cart line come from the catalogue? Gift cards and custom amounts are skipped.
3. Does the line's product sit in the collection? A category warning uses the collection's product list from the last sync.
4. Was it already carried on from on this sale? Only a change to the warning or its lines brings it back, unless it is set to always show.
5. Is the sale part paid? Part-paid sales skip the warnings.

Tests: `tests/cartwarnings.test.ts`.

pages.title: Customers
pages.summary: Adding a customer to a sale, finding or creating one, the Customers list, and how customers stay in step with Shopify.
pages.lead: A customer is optional. Adding one links the sale to them in Shopify and fills in their email or mobile for receipts.

sections.basic:
### Adding a customer to a sale
Use any of these:
- The **customer row** at the top of the cart (it says **Add customer**, or **Add a customer (optional)** when explanations are on).
- The **Customers** tile on the Quick Menu.
- **⋯ ▸ Create customer** on the cart, which opens the sheet ready to type a new one.
- The Checkout search box, which lists matching customers.
- In the guided checkout, the **Customer** step.

A sheet opens with a search box. Type part of a name, email or phone and tap the person. To take the customer off again, tap the **✕** beside their name on the cart.

```screen
title: Add customer
input: Search name, email or phone | aiden
row: Aiden | aiden@example.com · 0412 345 678
row: Aiden's Sister | sister@example.com
button: Search Shopify
primary: Create customer
note: Tap a person to attach them to the sale. Tap "Search Shopify" to find someone this register has not seen yet.
```

### If they are not in the list
Tap **Search Shopify** (or press Return) to look in your Shopify store, which finds people this register has not heard of yet. If they are really new, tap **Create customer**, fill in **First name**, **Last name**, **Email** and **Mobile**, then tap **Create & attach**. You need at least one of name, email or mobile ("Add at least a name, email or phone").

### What having a customer on the sale does
- Their name shows on the cart, on a saved cart, and on the receipt.
- **Email receipt** and **Text receipt** start with their email or mobile already filled in.
- The order in Shopify is linked to them.

### The Customers list
**More ▸ Customers** shows everyone this register knows about (not shown in Minimal mode). Type in the search box to narrow it down, and press Return to search Shopify too. Tap a person to see their email, mobile, how many orders they have had, how much they have spent, and any note. From there:
- **Start sale** puts them on the cart and takes you to Checkout.
- **Edit** changes their first name, last name, email, mobile or note.
- The **person-plus** button at the top adds a new customer.

If saving fails you see **Could not save customer** or **Could not create customer** with Shopify's reason, such as an email that is already used.
sections.deep:
### Two lists, one store
Shopify is where customers really live. Each register keeps a copy, loaded by **Settings ▸ Shopify ▸ Import from Shopify**, so searching is quick and works with a poor connection. That copy is not refreshed by the background check that keeps stock, saved carts and the Quick Menu in step. So:
- A customer you create or edit on this register shows up here straight away.
- On another register they appear after that register imports again, **or** after someone there taps **Search Shopify**.
- If you attach a customer found by **Search Shopify**, the sale uses them correctly, but they are not added to this register's list until the next import.

### What search covers
Local search looks in the name, email and mobile, and shows up to 30 people when the box is empty and up to 40 matches when it is not. **Search Shopify** adds up to 20 more, hiding anyone already shown. The Customers list shows up to 200.

### What is carried onto the sale
Only the customer's name, email and mobile go onto the cart. Order count and total spent are for looking at on the Customers list and are not saved with the sale.

### Editing a name
The Edit form splits the saved name at the first space: the first word is the first name and the rest is the last name. A name like "Mary Jane Smith" becomes First "Mary", Last "Jane Smith". Check it before saving.

### What the app cannot do
It cannot delete or merge customers. Do that in Shopify, then import again.

### Gift cards
When you sell a gift card to someone with an email address, the app looks for a Shopify customer with that email and creates one if there is none, because Shopify needs a customer to send the card to.
sections.advanced:
### From picking a customer to the Shopify order
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Customer row, tile or search] --> B[CustomerSheet in sheets.tsx]
  B -->|type| C[filter data.customers on this register]
  B -->|Search Shopify| D[searchRemote: customers first 20]
  B -->|Create customer| E[createCustomer: customerCreate]
  C --> F[onPick]
  D --> F
  E --> G[patchData adds to data.customers] --> F
  F --> H[setCart: customer id, name, email, phone]
  H --> I[saleBuilder.ts copies the customer onto the sale]
  I --> J[orderModel.ts: customer toAssociate id]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The picker and create form | `CustomerSheet` in `src/screens/sheets.tsx` (opened from `CartPane.tsx`, `Checkout.tsx` and `GuidedCheckout.tsx`) |
| The Customers screen | `src/screens/Customers.tsx` (`Customers`) |
| Shopify calls | `searchRemote`, `createCustomer`, `updateCustomer` in `src/lib/shopify/customers.ts` |
| The full import | `fetchCustomers` in `src/lib/shopify/catalogue.ts`, called from `importFromShopify` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| The local list | `data.customers` in `src/state/store.ts` (`patchData`) |
| What goes on a cart | `CustomerRef` in `src/lib/types.ts` (id, name, email, phone) |
| Linking the order | `orderModel.ts`: `customer: { toAssociate: { id } }` when the sale has a customer |
| Receipt prefill | `Receipt.tsx` uses `sale.customer?.email` and `sale.customer?.phone` |
| The button wording | `customerRowText` in `src/lib/simpleLabels.ts` |
| Whether the row is shown | `MORE_GROUPS`, `ROWS_BY_LEVEL` in `src/lib/uiMode.ts` (not in the Essential level) |
| Gift card recipients | `resolveRecipientId` in `src/lib/shopify/giftcards.ts` |
| Tests | `tests/simplelabels.test.ts` (the row wording). The customer calls themselves are not tested, because they need Shopify |

`customers.ts` maps a Shopify customer to `Customer` (`orders` from `numberOfOrders`, `spentCents` from `amountSpent`). `createCustomer` and `updateCustomer` drop empty fields and pass Shopify's `userErrors` to `throwUserErrors`, which is where the text in **Could not create customer** comes from.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **A customer made on another register is missing here.** The list is a copy. Import again in Settings ▸ Shopify, or tap **Search Shopify**.
- **The Customers list is empty.** The import has not run, or Shopify has no customers. Settings ▸ Shopify shows the counts from the last import.
- **Search Shopify finds nothing.** `searchRemote` takes Shopify's search syntax, so a typo or an exact-phone mismatch finds nothing. Try the email.
- **Could not create customer.** Read Shopify's reason in the message. An email or phone that is already used is the usual cause. Search for the existing person instead.
- **The receipt has no email filled in.** The customer has no email in Shopify, or the sale was started without a customer.
- **The Customers row is not on the More tab.** The staff member is on the Essential More level (Minimal, or a Custom setting). See `visibleMoreRows` in `src/lib/uiMode.ts`.

pages.title: The Quick Menu grid and editing it
pages.summary: Tiles, categories, display groups and pages on the Quick Menu, how to change them, and how the layout is shared and moved.
pages.lead: The Quick Menu is your own layout of buttons. You decide what is on it, how it is grouped, and what colour each button is.

sections.basic:
### What a tile can be
- **Item**: adds that product to the cart. If it has several variations you pick one first (see [[sales/variants-and-stock]]).
- **Category**: opens inside to show its own tiles, then every product in that Shopify collection. The photo on the tile is the collection's picture.
- **Display group**: a folder you fill yourself with any tiles you like. It can optionally act like a collection too.
- **Action**: a button that does a job: Custom amount, Sell gift card, Clear cart, Create item, Customers, Discounts, Cart discount, Saved carts, Switch staff, Lock POS, Price check, Stock check, Check change.
- **Discount**: applies a percentage or dollar discount to the whole cart.

A small dot on an item tile shows its stock: green is fine, amber is low (2 or fewer), red is oversold (below zero). No dot means the stock is not tracked.

### Moving around
When you open a category or group, a bar above the tiles shows where you are, for example *Home > Dragons > Highland cow*. Tap any earlier name to jump back to it, or use the back arrow to go up one step. Categories can sit inside categories as deep as you like.

```screen
title: Quick Menu
sub: Home > Dragons
tile: Highland Cow · Cream | $12.50
tile: Tadling · Green | $8.00
tile: Gemstone egg · Crushed Blue | $9.00
tile: !1 Cows | 24 items
tile: Sell gift card
tile: 10% off
note: A dot on an item tile shows its stock. Tapping a category tile takes you inside it.
```

### Changing the grid
1. On Checkout, with **Quick Menu** selected, tap the **pencil** at the top. It turns into a green tick.
2. **Tap a tile** to change it: its label, its colour, and for a category or group what it shows and what is inside it.
3. The **red minus** at a tile's top-left removes it. The **arrows** at its bottom-right move it earlier or later.
4. The dashed **+** tile adds something: Items, Categories, Display groups, Actions or Discounts.
5. Tap the green tick when you are done.

You are editing the level you are standing in. Open a category first to change what is inside it. Everything saves as you go, and your other registers get the change shortly afterwards.

### Pages
If you have more than one page, a row of page names sits above the tiles. While editing, a **Pages** button (or tapping the current page's name) opens a list where you can rename the page, add a new one, move pages up and down, or delete one. You cannot delete the last page.

### Tile size
Settings ▸ Theme ▸ **Tile size** (Small, Medium or Large) sets the tile size the grid aims for. The tiles are then stretched or squeezed a little, keeping their shape, so the columns fill the width beside the cart with no gap at the edge. If less than about half a tile of space would be left over, the tiles grow to use it. If more, the grid adds another column and the tiles shrink a little to fit it. The grid always has at least two columns.

### Missing tiles
A greyed tile saying **Missing item** or **Missing category** points at something that no longer exists in Shopify. Remove the tile, or import your products again in Settings ▸ Shopify if it should still be there.

### Moving a layout in or out
Settings ▸ **Grid import / export** lets you paste or pick a `grid.json` file, export your grid, or push the layout to your other registers right now. Any tile that cannot be understood is skipped, and you are told how many.
sections.deep:
### Category or display group?
A **category** is tied to a Shopify collection. Open it and you see the tiles you put inside it first (usually sub-categories), then the products in the collection. A **display group** is just your own folder with its own tiles. If you switch on "Acts like a collection" for a group, it shows that collection's products after its tiles, like a category does.

### Which products show where
If a product belongs to both a category and one of that category's sub-categories (at any depth), it only shows in the deepest one. This stops the same product appearing in every level. A product you pin yourself as an **Item** tile is never hidden by this, and it is not shown twice in the same place.

### One product or one variation
An Item tile can point at a whole product (the picker appears if it has several variations) or at one specific variation (it is added straight away). Tiles you add from a product use the whole product.

### What editing shows
While editing, a category shows only the tiles stored inside it, not its collection's products, because those are filled in automatically and cannot be moved. A note under the grid says so.

### Shared between registers
The layout is stored in Shopify, so every register shows the same grid. After you change something, the new layout is sent about a second and a half later. Each register checks for a newer layout about every 25 seconds while the app is open, and when it returns to the front. A layout that cannot be read is ignored, so a bad import cannot blank another register.
sections.advanced:
### The data
```text
{ "version": 1, "pages": [ { "id": "...", "name": "Home", "tiles": [ ... ] } ] }
```
A tile is one of five shapes, from `src/lib/grid.ts`:

| `type` | Fields |
|---|---|
| `action` | `action` (one of `ACTIONS`), optional `label`, `color` |
| `category` | `collectionId`, optional `label`, `color`, `subs` (more tiles) |
| `item` | `variantId` or `productId`, optional `label`, `color` |
| `discount` | `code`, `pct` or `amtCents`, optional `label`, `color` |
| `group` | `name`, `tiles`, optional `collectionId`, `color` |

`parseGrid` accepts a JSON string or object, drops any tile that fails `isTile` (counting them in `dropped`), and always returns at least one page. A new install gets `defaultGrid()`: one Home page with every action except Cart discount.

### Paths and nesting
`src/lib/gridNav.ts` is pure and works on a **path**: a list of tile indexes, one per level (`[2, 0]` is tile 2 on the page, then tile 0 inside it). `resolvePath` walks it and stops at the first step that no longer exists, so a layout change from another register cannot leave a screen pointing at nothing. `listAt`, `editListAt`, `updateTileAt`, `addTileAt`, `removeTileAt` and `moveTileAt` return changed copies and never edit in place.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  P[path from Checkout state] --> R[resolvePath]
  R --> E{editing?}
  E -->|yes| C[childTiles of the last container]
  E -->|no| V[viewTiles: own tiles, then ownProductIds items]
  C --> G[TileGrid]
  V --> G
  G -->|tap a container| O[onOpen: path plus index]
  G -->|tap an item| A[handlers.onVariants]
```

`ownProductIds` implements the deepest-wins rule: it removes any product found in `descendantCollectionIds`. `viewTiles` also skips a product already pinned as an item tile inside the container. `breadcrumbs` builds the bar from the resolved nodes.

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Edit mode, page chips, path state | `Checkout.tsx` (`editing`, `pageIdx`, `path`, `edit`, `editPage`) |
| Drawing tiles, the add sheet | `Tiles.tsx` (`TileGrid`, `TileView`, `AddTileSheet`) |
| Tile settings sheet | `TileSettings.tsx` (`TileSettingsSheet`) |
| Saving and sharing | `commitGrid` in `Tiles.tsx` (saves at once, `pushLayout` after 1.5 s) |
| Push and pull | `pushLayout`, `pullLayout` in `src/lib/sync.ts`; stored in the `pos_layout` metaobject with a `version` |
| Import and export | `GridSettings` in `Settings.tsx` |
| Tile size to fit the pane | `tileColumnsForPane`, `tileSizeForPane` in `src/lib/gridLayout.ts`; the pane is measured by `TileGrid` in `Tiles.tsx` |
| Tests | `tests/gridnav.test.ts`, `tests/gridlayout.test.ts` |

### Reading the code for a fault
- **A gap at the right edge of the grid.** The tile width is the pane width minus 16 points of padding, divided by the column count and rounded down to a quarter point, so at most a point or so per column can be left over. A bigger gap means the pane was measured wrong: `TileGrid` reports its own width through `onLayout`, and until it has reported, the grid guesses from the window width.
- **A change did not reach another register.** `pullLayout` only applies a layout whose `version` is higher than that register's `gridVersion`. Check the register is online (the strip on Checkout), then Settings ▸ Grid import / export ▸ Push layout now.
- **Items missing from a category.** Either the collection has no products on this device (import again) or the products also sit in a sub-category (`ownProductIds`).
- **Import said "N unsupported tiles skipped".** Those failed `isTile`: an unknown `type`, an `action` that is not in `ACTIONS`, or an item with neither `variantId` nor `productId`.

pages.title: Lock POS, Price check and Stock check
pages.summary: The three Quick Menu buttons that do not sell anything: lock the register, look up a price and its deals, look up stock.
pages.lead: These buttons are for looking, not selling. Price check and Stock check never touch the cart, and Lock POS leaves it exactly as it is.

sections.basic:
### Lock POS
Tap the **Lock POS** tile when you step away. The register goes to the **Sign in** screen. The sale you were ringing up is still there when someone signs back in, with a PIN or by scanning a cashier pass.

You may see one of these instead of the lock:
| Message | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **No staff set up** | Nobody has a PIN yet, so there would be no way back in. | Add a staff member in More ▸ Staff first. |
| **Payment in progress** | A card payment is waiting on the reader. | Finish or cancel it, then lock. |
| **Already locked** | The register is already on the Sign in screen. | Nothing to do. |

There is also **Lock register** in the More tab. It appears when your register asks for PINs and has staff set up.

### Price check
Tap **Price check** to open a full-screen sheet. Then do one of these:
- Scan an item with the Bluetooth scanner.
- Tap **Scan with camera** and scan it. The camera closes after a good scan.
- Type a name, SKU or barcode in the search box and tap the item.

You see the photo, the name, the price in big numbers, and the stock. If the item has a higher "compare at" price, that is shown crossed out beside it. Under that, **Deals this item can be part of** lists any automatic discount or bundle deal the item is in. If it says **Excluded from discounts**, no deal will ever apply to it.

Those deals are a hint. Minimum quantities still apply, so the cart shows the real price. Scan the next item and it replaces the last one. Tap **Clear** to start again.

### Stock check
Tap **Stock check** and find an item the same way. You see how many are in stock, then the **other variations** of the same product with their prices and counts. A line at the bottom adds them up, for example "14 in stock across all 3 variations". If the product has only one variation it says **This product has no other variations.**

Stock words mean what they do on the grid (see [[sales/variants-and-stock]]): **12 in stock**, **Out of stock**, **3 oversold**, **Not tracked**.

### If a scan shows a message
- **No item for …** and the code: nothing matches that barcode or SKU. See [[sales/scanners]].
- **That is a cashier pass, not an item.** You scanned a staff pass.
- **That is a gift card. Check its balance from Charge ▸ Gift card.** You scanned a gift card QR.
sections.deep:
### Why Lock POS will not lock during a card payment
A card payment that was started in the last five minutes and has not finished counts as "waiting on the reader". Locking then would hide the till while the customer is tapping their card, so it waits. After five minutes the attempt stops counting, so a payment that was abandoned does not block locking for ever. Switching to another staff member follows the same rule.

### What locking keeps
Locking only signs the person out. The cart, a half-finished payment on the cart and a saved cart are all left alone. The screensaver can also appear sooner on the Sign in screen than on a signed-in register, if that is switched on in Settings.

### What Price check shows, and what it does not
The price is the item's own price from your last import. It is not the price after deals. A deal is listed when:
- it is an automatic discount that is inside its dates, or a bundle deal that is switched on and inside its dates,
- and the item, its product or one of its collections is part of it. For a "buy this, get that" deal either side counts.

An item tagged `no-discount` never lists a deal. Because quantities are ignored, an item can list a "3 for $20" deal when you have only one. That is expected.

### What the Stock check total adds up
Only counts that are tracked are added, and a negative count is treated as 0, so oversold items do not pull the total down. Variations that are not tracked are mentioned in brackets after the total.

### Typed searches
A search shows one row per product, and every word you type must appear in the name, variation, SKU or barcode. It stops at 30 products. In Stock check, a row also says how many variations the product has.
sections.advanced:
### What happens on a scan or a pick
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[Scan or typed code] --> R[resolveScan in lookup.ts]
  R -->|barcode or SKU matches| V[variant found]
  R -->|cashier pass| P[scanProblem: That is a cashier pass]
  R -->|gift card QR| G[scanProblem: check from Charge, Gift card]
  R -->|nothing| N[scanProblem: No item for code]
  V --> M{mode}
  M -->|price| PR[priceCheck then PriceResult]
  M -->|stock| ST[stockCheck then StockResult]
```

### What happens on Lock POS
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  T[Lock POS tile] --> L[lockNow in staffAuth.ts]
  L --> D{lockDecision in posLock.ts}
  D -->|no staff| A1[alert: No staff set up]
  D -->|already locked| A2[alert: Already locked]
  D -->|card payment waiting| A3[alert: Payment in progress]
  D -->|ok| K[lockRegister clears unlocked and staffId]
  K --> E[csv event staff_switch, locked from the grid]
  K --> U[App.tsx shows PinLock because isLockScreen is true]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The tiles | `Checkout.tsx`: the `lock_pos`, `price_check` and `stock_check` cases open `lockNow`, or the Price or Stock sheet |
| The sheet, scanner and results | `src/screens/Lookup.tsx` (`LookupSheet`, `PriceResult`, `StockResult`) |
| Scan resolution and messages | `resolveScan`, `scanProblem` in `src/lib/lookup.ts` |
| Price and deals | `priceCheck`, `dealsFor` in `src/lib/lookup.ts` (`dealLive` in `src/lib/bundles.ts`, `NO_DISCOUNT_TAG` in `src/lib/pricing.ts`) |
| Stock tone, words, totals | `stockToneOf`, `stockText`, `stockCheck` in `src/lib/lookup.ts` |
| Typed search | `searchVariants` in `src/lib/lookup.ts` |
| The lock rules | `lockDecision`, `isLockScreen` in `src/lib/posLock.ts` |
| Locking and signing back in | `lockNow`, `lockRegister`, `signInWithPin`, `signInWithPass` in `src/lib/staffAuth.ts`; `PinLock` in `src/screens/Staff.tsx` |
| The five-minute card rule | `paymentActive` in `src/lib/screensaver.ts` |
| The More row | `visibleMoreRows` in `src/lib/uiMode.ts`, which hides **Lock register** unless PINs are required and staff exist |
| Tests | `tests/lookup.test.ts` |

`resolveScan` checks barcodes and SKUs first, then cashier passes, then gift QRs, so a real barcode always wins. The sheet's scanner is `HidScanner enabled={visible && !cam}`, so it listens only while the sheet is open and the camera is closed. Each new result replaces the old one.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **Lock POS says "No staff set up".** `settings.staff` is empty on this register. Staff are shared between registers, so check that the settings pulled in (Settings ▸ Shopify, and the sync strip on Checkout).
- **Lock POS says "Payment in progress" with nothing on the reader.** An entry in `pos.attempts` has the status `started` and is under five minutes old. Finish or cancel the payment on the Pay screen, or wait out the window.
- **Locked, but the old cart is gone after signing in.** Locking never clears the cart. Look for a sale that was paid or a cart that was cleared.
- **Price check shows no deal you expected.** Is the item tagged `no-discount`? Is the discount inside its dates? Is the item, its product or one of its collections in the discount's target? For a bundle, is it switched on, in date, and is the variation or product in one of its sets?
- **A scan finds nothing.** The scan path is shared with Checkout, so use the fault list on [[sales/scanners]].
- **Stock differs from Shopify.** See [[sales/variants-and-stock]].

pages.title: Saved carts
pages.summary: Park a sale to finish later, find it again on any register, merge it into another cart, and how saved carts are shared.
pages.lead: A saved cart is a sale put on hold: the items, the customer and a name, kept so you can come back to it. Every register sees the same saved carts.

sections.basic:
### Saving a cart
1. Put the items in the cart (add a customer if you like).
2. Tap **⋯** on the cart and choose **Save cart**.
3. Give it a name, such as *Sam, holding for Friday*, and add a note if you want. If you leave the name blank it uses the customer's name, or "Cart" with the time.
4. Tap **Save to Saved carts**. The cart is now empty and ready for the next customer.

You cannot save an empty cart ("Cart is empty"), or a cart that has had part of its payment taken ("Payment in progress").

### Finding and opening one
Open **More ▸ Saved carts**, or tap the **Saved carts** tile on the Quick Menu. Each row shows the name, how many items, the total, the customer, and any note. You can also type a name, note or customer in the Checkout search box and pick the **Saved carts** filter.

```screen
title: Saved carts
input: Search | friday
row: Sam, holding for Friday | 3 items · $28.50
text: For Aiden · Note: call when ready
row: Walk-in order | 1 item · $12.50
button: Open
button: Assign → Aiden
primary: Delete
note: Tap a saved cart to open, assign or delete it.
```

Tap a cart to see what is in it, then:
- **Open**: if your cart is empty the saved cart goes straight in. If it already has items you are asked **Merge Carts?**, and choosing **Merge** adds the saved items to what is already there.
- **Assign → name**: marks the cart as meant for that staff member. Their name appears on the row. It is a label only: anyone can still open it.
- **Delete**: asks "Delete saved cart?" first. It is removed from every register.

On the list you can also **swipe a row** to delete it. You are asked to confirm, and the row slides back if you say no.

### Good to know
- Opening a saved cart does not use it up. It stays in the list until the sale made from it is paid, then it is removed for you.
- A **whole order price** is not kept in a saved cart. The Save cart sheet warns you, and the cart comes back at its normal total.
- A row that says **not synced** has not reached the other registers yet. It sends as soon as the register is online.
sections.deep:
### How carts are shared
Saved carts are kept in your Shopify store, so any register can open them. A register sends its changes straight away, and every register checks for new or changed carts about every 25 seconds while the app is open. The cart you saved a moment ago may take up to that long to appear on another register.

If a register is offline, the cart is kept on that register (marked **not synced**) and sent when the connection returns. Until then, that register's copy wins over anything newer that arrives for the same cart, so your own unsent change is never overwritten.

### Deleting
Deleting marks the cart as void. Other registers drop it at their next check. There is no "undo", and nothing is asked a second time on the other registers.

### Open into an empty cart, or merge
- **Empty cart:** the saved items, customer and cart discount replace it. Any half-made payment details are cleared, so a saved cart can never bring a payment with it.
- **Cart with items:** the saved lines are added. If **Consolidate identical items** is on, the same item combines into one line, except lines that have been changed (a changed price, a discount, a note or an adjustment), which stay separate. Your current cart's customer and discount are kept, and the saved cart's are used only if the current cart has none. If any line in the merged cart has a price adjustment, the whole order price is dropped.

### Two registers, one cart
There is no lock on a saved cart. If two registers change the same one at nearly the same moment, the one that sends last wins. For a shop with a few registers this is rare, but it is a good reason to **Open** a cart rather than edit it in two places.
sections.advanced:
### From Save cart to another register
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Save cart sheet: SaveCartSheet in sheets.tsx] --> B[saveCartLocal in sync.ts: dirty true]
  B --> C[pushSaved: meta.upsert to pos_saved_cart]
  C -->|sent| D[dirty false, remoteId and version stored]
  C -->|offline| E[stays dirty, App.tsx 25 s tick retries]
  F[pollShared every 25 s] --> G[pullSaved: meta.list first 100]
  G -->|local copy dirty| H[keep local]
  G -->|status void| I[remove locally]
  G -->|open| J[replace or add local copy]
  K[Open: openSavedCart in savedOps.ts] --> L{current cart empty?}
  L -->|yes| M[setCart with savedFrom set]
  L -->|no| N[confirm Merge Carts then mergeCarts in cartOps.ts]
  M --> O[Pay.tsx on a paid sale: updateSaved savedFrom void]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Save sheet (clears the cart after saving) | `SaveCartSheet` in `src/screens/sheets.tsx`; its `onSaved` empties the cart in `CartPane.tsx` and `GuidedCheckout.tsx` |
| The list, Open, Assign, Delete, swipe | `src/screens/SavedCarts.tsx` (`SavedCarts`, `SwipeRow` in `src/ui/SwipeRow.tsx`) |
| Open, delete, assign | `openSavedCart`, `deleteSavedCart`, `assignSavedCart` in `src/lib/savedOps.ts` |
| Saving and syncing | `saveCartLocal`, `updateSaved`, `pushSaved`, `pullSaved`, `cartFields` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| The stored shape | `SavedCart` in `src/state/store.ts`; the `pos_saved_cart` definition in `src/lib/shopify/metaobjects.ts` (`ensureDefinitions`) |
| Merging | `mergeCarts` in `src/lib/cartOps.ts` |
| Removing a used cart | the `savedFrom` check in `Pay.tsx` |
| Search filter | the `carts` results in `Checkout.tsx` |
| The 25 second tick | `App.tsx` (`pollShared`, `pushSaved`) |

A saved cart stores `lines_json`, `discount_json` and `customer_json` along with the name, note, employee, register and a `version`. `SaveCartSheet` strips the cart's own name and `orderAdjust` before saving, which is why a whole order price does not survive. Assigning writes the status as `assigned:` followed by the staff id, and `pullSaved` reads it back. Nothing else reads that field.

`pullSaved` asks for up to 100 carts. A cart that is deleted elsewhere and is not in that list is left alone, because the code does not guess about deletions. The `locked_by` and `locked_at` fields exist in the Shopify definition but nothing writes them yet.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **A cart saved on one register is missing on another.** On the saving register, look for **not synced**: it is still `dirty`. Otherwise check the other register's sync strip, and that Settings ▸ Shopify ▸ **Set up shared storage (metaobjects)** was run (it creates `pos_saved_cart`).
- **A deleted cart came back.** The register that still had it was offline with its own copy marked dirty, and sent it on reconnecting.
- **Saved, but the whole order price is gone.** Working as designed (see `SaveCartSheet`).
- **A saved cart is still listed after the sale was paid.** The sale was made from a merged cart, not an opened one: only `openSavedCart` into an empty cart sets `savedFrom`. Delete the saved cart by hand.
- **Merge made two lines of the same item.** One had a changed price, discount, note or adjustment, so `mergeCarts` keeps them apart.
- **Tests.** There is no test for the saved cart sync itself. `mergeCarts` is covered in `tests/itemadjust.test.ts` and `tests/lineadjust.test.ts`.

pages.title: Scanning items, passes and gift cards
pages.summary: The Bluetooth scanner and the camera, what a scan does on each screen, and what to do when scanning misbehaves.
pages.lead: A scan is the quickest way to add an item. The POS understands four kinds of code: item barcodes and SKUs, cashier passes, gift card QR codes and saved discount codes. It always checks them in that order, so an item is never mistaken for anything else.

sections.basic:
### The two scanners
- **Bluetooth scanner.** Pair it in the iPad's own Settings as a keyboard (HID mode). After that, on Checkout, just scan: the item goes in the cart.
- **Camera.** Tap the camera icon next to the search bar. A full-screen camera opens and stays open, so you can scan several things in a row. Each scan shows a green message ("Added Dragon plush") or a red one ("Not found: …"). Tap **Done** when finished. The camera reads EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, Code 128, Code 39, ITF-14 and QR codes.

The gift card pop-up (Charge ▸ Gift card) has its own camera button for scanning a gift card's QR code.

To check a Bluetooth scanner is working, go to Settings ▸ **Hardware** and scan something. The last few scans are listed and nothing is added to any cart. See [[settings/hardware]] for the test steps.

### What a scan does, by screen
| Where you are | Item barcode or SKU | Cashier pass | Gift card QR | Discount code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Checkout** (grid and cart side by side, or the cart page) | Adds 1 to the cart | Signs that person in; the cart stays as it is | Opens the cart's gift card window with the balance | Applies the discount to the cart |
| **Price check / Stock check** | Shows its price or stock; the cart is not touched | "That is a cashier pass, not an item." | Tells you to check it from Charge ▸ Gift card | "That is a discount code, not an item." |
| **Staff sign-in** | Not accepted | Signs in | Not accepted | Not accepted |

With the grid and the cart side by side there is one scan box, not two, so a scan always goes through the same order. An item comes first: a product whose SKU is a web address (`https://…`) is found as an item.

If nothing matches (not an item, pass, gift card or saved discount) you see **No item for** followed by the code. Fix that in Shopify (see Advanced for the usual causes).

### When scanning does nothing
- A pop-up is open, or you are on another screen (such as Pay). Scanning only adds to the cart from the Checkout screen with nothing on top of it.
- You were typing in a box a moment ago. Scans are ignored for about 2½ seconds after you finish typing, so the scanner cannot take over what you were typing.
- The scanner is not paired or not in keyboard mode. Test it in Settings ▸ Hardware.

### Getting the on-screen keyboard back
A Bluetooth scanner stops the iPad showing its on-screen keyboard. On the POS-mate scanner, **double-click the scanner button** to show the keyboard, and double-click again to hide it.
sections.deep:
### How a code is matched
The code is compared with each variation's **barcode** after removing spaces and any zeros at the start. That is why a 12-digit UPC and the 13-digit EAN that begins with 0 find the same item. If no barcode matches, the code is tried against each **SKU** exactly, ignoring capital letters. If two items share a barcode, the first one found wins, so keep barcodes unique.

### The order things are checked
Checkout asks "is it a cashier pass?" first, then "is it an item?", then "is it a gift card?". The Price check and Stock check pop-ups ask "is it an item?" first, so a real barcode always wins there. A pass is the letter P followed by 12 letters and digits. A gift card QR starts with `shopify-giftcard-v1-`. Because no item should ever look like either, the order rarely matters.

### Why a scanner acts like a keyboard
A Bluetooth scanner connected this way pretends to be a keyboard: it types the digits and then presses Return. The POS keeps a hidden, always-ready text box that catches those keystrokes, and treats Return as "scan finished". This is also why a scanner can fight with a real keyboard, and why the POS backs off while you type.

### Two scans of the same code
The camera ignores the same code if it is seen again within about a second, so holding the camera on one barcode does not add ten.
sections.advanced:
### The path of a scan
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  K[Scanner types code and Return] --> H[HidScanner hidden TextInput]
  H -->|onSubmitEditing| S[onScan code]
  C[CameraScanner onBarcodeScanned] -->|same code within 1.2 s ignored| S
  S --> F[findByBarcode: barcode then SKU]
  F -->|found| A[add 1, toast Added]
  F -->|not found| B{isBadgeCode?}
  B -->|yes| P[signInWithPass, cart unchanged]
  B -->|no| G{isGiftQr?}
  G -->|yes| M[cart gift card window with balance]
  G -->|no| D{saved discount label?}
  D -->|yes| X[apply cart discount]
  D -->|no| N[toast: No item for code]
```

### Where the code is
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Hidden keyboard capture, camera screen | `src/screens/Scanner.tsx` (`HidScanner`, `CameraScanner`) |
| When Checkout listens | `Checkout.tsx`: `HidScanner enabled={active && nav.tab === 'checkout' && sheet === 'none' && !cam && !cartBlocked && nav.stack.length === 0}`; `cartBlocked` is true while a cart window is open beside the grid |
| One box beside the grid | `CartPane hid={false}` gives up its own box; it registers with `registerCartScan` in `src/lib/scanBridge.ts` so Checkout can hand it gift card and discount scans and see when one of its windows is open. On the phone's cart page the pane keeps its own box (`scanAll` in `CartPane.tsx`) |
| Matching | `findByBarcode`, `normaliseBarcode` in `src/lib/cartOps.ts` (strips whitespace and leading zeros; then SKU, lower-cased) |
| Order, pass, gift, discount, none | `resolveScan`, `findDiscountPreset`, `scanProblem` in `src/lib/lookup.ts`; `isBadgeCode`, `cleanScan`, `BADGE_RE` (`/^P[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{12}$/`) in `src/lib/badge.ts`; `isGiftQr` in `src/lib/giftCode.ts` |
| Not stealing the keyboard | `src/lib/focusGuard.ts` (`isUserTyping`, `TYPING_GRACE_MS` = 2500); every `Field` calls `fieldFocused` and `fieldBlurred` |
| Price and Stock check | `src/screens/Lookup.tsx` (`HidScanner enabled={visible && !cam}`) |
| Sign-in screen | `src/screens/StaffLogin.tsx` (only passes accepted) |
| Hardware test and speed test | `HardwareTest` in `src/screens/ScannerSpeed.tsx` (keeps the last 8 scans) |
| Tests | `tests/focusguard.test.ts`, `tests/lookup.test.ts`, `tests/scanorder.test.ts` |

### How HidScanner keeps focus
It only takes focus when `isUserTyping()` is false and `Keyboard.isVisible()` is false. It tries on mount and then every 1.5 seconds if it has lost focus. The text box is 1 pixel, almost invisible, hides the soft keyboard (`showSoftInputOnFocus={false}`), and is replaced (new `key`) after every scan so the old text can never leak into the next code. The code used is `nativeEvent.text`, falling back to the last typed value, trimmed.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **"No item for …" on a real product.** The variation has no `barcode` or `sku` on this device, or the value differs by more than spaces and leading zeros. A Shopify barcode with letters or a dash will not match a scan without them. Fix it in Shopify, then import again in Settings ▸ Shopify.
- **Scan works in Settings ▸ Hardware but not on Checkout.** One of the conditions in the `enabled` expression is false: a sheet is open (including a cart window beside the grid), the camera is up, a screen is stacked on top, or the tab is not Checkout.
- **Scan is ignored just after typing.** Working as designed (`TYPING_GRACE_MS`). Wait about 2½ seconds.
- **The keyboard disappears while typing.** That was a bug fixed in patch 0001; if it returns, check that the input in question is a kit `Field` (a raw `TextInput` is invisible to the guard, though `Keyboard.isVisible()` still covers it).
- **The same item is added twice.** The scanner sent the code twice, or its trigger was held. The camera path de-duplicates within 1.2 seconds; the Bluetooth path does not.
- **Characters come out wrong.** The scanner's keyboard layout does not match the iPad's. Change it with the scanner's setup barcodes, not in the app.

pages.title: Variations, stock counts and negative stock
pages.summary: Choosing a variation, what the stock dots and words mean, why you can sell below zero, and how counts stay up to date.
pages.lead: A product can come in several variations, such as colour or size. Each variation has its own price and its own stock count.

sections.basic:
### Choosing a variation
Tap a product that has more than one variation and the grid is replaced by one tile per variation. Each shows its photo, name, price and stock. Tap the one you want and it goes in the cart, and you are back where you were. The bar above shows the product as the last step, for example *Home > Dragons > Highland cow*, so tap an earlier name to leave without choosing.

A product with only one variation skips this step and is added straight away.

```screen
title: Highland cow
sub: Home > Dragons > Highland cow
tile: Grey | $12.50
tile: !1 Cream | $12.50
tile: Ginger | $13.00
note: Tapping a tile adds that variation to the cart and returns to the grid.
```

### What the stock words mean
| You see | It means |
|---|---|
| **12 in stock** | There are 12 counted. |
| **Out of stock** | The count is 0. |
| **3 oversold** | The count is below zero: 3 more have been sold than were counted. |
| **Not tracked** | This item has no stock count (a service, or tracking is off in Shopify). |

The coloured dot follows the same idea: green is fine, amber is 2 or fewer (including 0), and red is oversold.

### Selling when stock is 0
You can always sell an item that shows 0 or below. The POS warns you ("stock will go negative") and carries on, because the shelf is the truth and the count may simply be behind.

### When the count changes
- Selling an item lowers its count straight away on this device.
- A refund puts it back.
- Counts also change when someone on another register or in Shopify changes them. The app checks about every 25 seconds while it is open.
- If any item goes below zero, a notification appears in the Notifications tab that takes you to Inventory so you can fix the count.

### Fixing a wrong count
Counts are corrected in Inventory (set a count, receive stock, or adjust it). If many items look wrong after a busy day, check that sales are not queued: the strip on Checkout says "Offline" or "queued" when they are.
sections.deep:
### Why overselling is allowed
Shopify is told to take the stock off even if that makes it negative. A till that refused to sell would stop a customer who is standing there with the item in their hand, so the rule is: sell first, correct the count after.

### Not tracked
A variation whose stock is "not tracked" never shows a dot, is never counted in totals, and is not changed by sales or refunds. This is not the same as 0.

### Stock check totals
The Stock check tile shows the scanned variation first, then its siblings, and a total. The total only adds counts that are tracked, and treats negative counts as 0, so oversold stock does not pull the total down. It also says how many variations are not tracked, in brackets after the total.

### Several registers
Each register keeps its own copy of the counts and applies its own sales at once, so the number you see is right for you immediately. The real number lives in Shopify and each register catches up every 25 seconds or so. Two registers selling the last item at the same moment will both succeed, and the count will go to -1.
sections.advanced:
### Data and thresholds
`Variant.stock` is `number | null` (`null` = not tracked). The thresholds are in two places that agree: `stockToneOf` in `src/lib/lookup.ts` (`none`, `ok`, `low` at 1 to 2, `out` at 0, `neg` below 0) and `stockTone` in `src/state/selectors.ts` for the tile dot (which has no separate `out`, so 0 shows as low).

### When stock moves
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Add an item] --> B{stock tracked and stock minus qty below 0?}
  B -->|yes| W[toast: stock will go negative]
  B -->|no| T[toast: Added item]
  S[Sale completes] --> L[applyLocalStock: sync.ts]
  L --> O[outbox: Shopify orderCreate with DECREMENT_IGNORING_POLICY]
  O --> H[Shopify lowers the stock]
  P[pollShared every 25 s] --> D[fetchStockDelta since stockSince]
  D --> U[variants stock replaced from Shopify]
```

- `applyLocalStock` changes the local count for each sold line by `-qty` for a sale, `+qty` for a refund, skipping untracked variations.
- Shopify's own count is lowered by the order itself (`DECREMENT_IGNORING_POLICY`), so the POS does not send a second adjustment for sales.
- For refunds the outbox item carries `done: { order, stock }` and the stock step uses `adjustStock` in `src/lib/shopify/inventory.ts` (`inventoryAdjustQuantities` with an idempotency key, so a retry cannot apply twice).
- `pollShared` fetches stock changes since `stockSince` and replaces the matching variants' counts. Remote values win, which is how the count is corrected after a manual change in Shopify.
- `App.tsx` runs a 25-second tick that polls, empties the outbox, and raises the "N item(s) with negative stock" notice (route `inventory`).

### The picker
`VariantPicker` in `Tiles.tsx` draws one tile per variation using `pickerVariants` (catalogue order, no duplicate ids) and `stockText`. It is a level of the grid, not a popup: `pickerCrumbs` adds the product as the last crumb, and changing tab, page, path or edit mode closes it (the `useEffect` that calls `setVariants(null)` in `Checkout.tsx`).

### Reading the code for a fault
- **Count did not drop after a sale.** The variation is untracked (`stock === null`), or `inventoryItemId` is missing so a later `pollShared` cannot match it. Check the variant on the device.
- **Count jumped back after a sale.** `pollShared` replaced it with Shopify's number; the order has probably not reached Shopify yet (outbox not empty).
- **Stock dot differs from the picker word.** Expected at exactly 0: the tile dot is amber for low, the picker says Out of stock.
- **Tests.** `tests/lookup.test.ts` covers the tones, the words, the stock check totals and the picker helpers.

pages.title: Settings
pages.summary: Find Shopify, payment, hardware, data, receipt, backup, display and other register settings.
pages.lead: Open **More ▸ Settings** to configure Shopify, payments, discounts, hardware and this register. Tap a section to open it; use the back button to return to the Settings list.

sections.basic:
### Find a setting
- **Shopify** connects the register to your shop; see [[settings/shopify]].
- **Payments** contains cash rounding, Smart change and card fee estimates; see [[settings/payments]].
- **Discounts & bundles** manages the bundle deals used in Checkout.
- **Cart warnings** sets the prompts shown at Charge for chosen items or categories. See [[sales/cart-warnings]].
- **Hardware** opens the scanner test; see [[settings/hardware]].
- **Data** exports chosen records as CSV files or a spreadsheet, shares the raw CSV files, or deletes local history.
- **Square history** imports old Square sales for Reports.
- **Grid import / export** moves the Checkout tile layout.
- **AI assistant** (owners, or managers when there is no owner) sets the model the Help assistant will use. See [[settings/assistant]].
- **Gift cards** has the claim-page and cashier-pass server settings.
- **Receipts** configures receipt and tax-invoice details; see [[settings/receipts]].
- **Backup & transfer** moves settings and logins to another device; **Data** exports or deletes local CSV history. See [[settings/backup]].
- **Screensaver & display** controls this iPad's idle screen and Keep iPad awake; see [[staff/screensaver]].
- **Theme** changes the app's appearance; see [[settings/theme]]. **About** shows app information.

The Settings list also has Checkout options for consolidating identical items and the tax display. Managers and Owners can access Settings when staff sign-in is required; cashiers cannot.
sections.deep:
### Settings are not all shared the same way
Some choices apply only to this register, such as Smart change and Screensaver & display. Shared settings, such as staff and bundle deals, sync with the other registers. The screen or setting guide explains when a choice is local.

The Payments section shows fee rates used for estimates. Zeller does not report actual card fees to the POS, and the automatic cash tender machine is still under construction; cash is entered and given by hand.
sections.advanced:
### Settings sections
| Section | Component or route |
|---|---|
| Settings list and section navigation | `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Shopify connection and catalogue import | `ShopifySettings` in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Payments, fees and cash rounding | Payments section in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Bundle deals | `BundlesEditor` in `src/screens/BundleBuilder.tsx` |
| Hardware scanner test | `HardwareTest` in `src/screens/ScannerSpeed.tsx` |
| Screensaver and display | `DisplaySettings` in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Settings model and defaults | `src/state/store.ts` |

Each section is a panel within the Settings screen. Its values may be stored locally, shared with the other registers, or held in the iPad's secure storage depending on the setting.

pages.title: Ask the assistant
pages.summary: Chat with the Help assistant: what it can and cannot do, asking about products, stock, sales, orders, deals, customers, gift cards how the till is doing, the cash drawer, the sale in progress and cash sums, what is kept, and what is hidden before anything is sent.
pages.lead: Open **Help** and tap the sparkles button at the top. For now only an owner can see it, or a manager when the team has no owner. It is not on the sign in screen, because your chat history belongs to you and the till needs to know who you are. Set up the model first: see [[settings/assistant]].

sections.basic:
### What it can do
Type a question and tap the round **Send** arrow beside the box. While the chat is empty it also offers a few questions to start with: tap one to ask it. It answers in plain words, in the language you write in. For how-to questions it looks through the till's help pages first (search, then read the best page), and answers from what it finds. For where-is-it questions it also looks through the till's screens and tells you the taps to get there, starting from the Checkout tab. If it finds nothing, it says so. It only looks at help pages and screens for things your role can use.

### How replies look
The assistant's replies are laid out the way it writes them: headings, **bold** and *slanted* words, bullet and numbered lists, tables and boxes of code. A small round badge marks each of its messages, and the time is shown under each message. Press and hold on a reply to select and copy its words. Links are never tappable in a reply: if it names a page or a screen, use the button under the reply instead.

### Buttons under a reply
When it points you at a help page or a screen, it can put a button under its reply. Tap **Open Reports**, for example, and you go straight there. A help page button opens that page in Help. Back returns you to the chat. Only tabs and ordinary pages get a button. A window that opens on top of something else, such as the refund window, has no button, so the reply gives you the taps instead. Short questions get short answers. Tap **More detail** under a reply for a fuller one.

### Guide me to a screen
Ask to be shown or walked to a screen (*Show me how to get to Reports*) and the reply can have a **Guide me to Reports** button. Tap it and the till goes to the Checkout tab and points at each button to tap, one at a time: a glowing ring on the button, and a small card that says what to do and which step you are on. Tap the button it points at, and it moves on to the next. When you arrive the card says *You are there*. It never dims the screen and never stops you tapping anything else. If you are already part of the way there, it picks up from where you are. Tap **Stop** on the card at any time. If it cannot see the next button (you went somewhere else), the card says so and you can go back to the Checkout tab or tap **Stop**. Only one guide runs at a time, it ends by itself after ten minutes, and it ends if someone else signs in. It only offers a guide to screens your role can reach, and to the others it says it could not find anything, just as it does for a screen that does not exist. A window that opens on top of something else, such as the refund window, has no guide, because the ring cannot be drawn above a window. The reply gives you the taps in words instead. A few pages have no guide either, because the button on the way to them cannot be pointed at (an item in the Items list, or Start on a training lesson). The Checkout tab has none, because that is where every guide starts.

### It knows where you were
When you open the chat from a page, it knows which tab or page that was, and how your till is set up: your role, your display mode and which tabs that mode shows. So *What is this screen for?* is answered about the page you came from, and it will not tell you to tap a tab your mode hides. It cannot see which window was open on top of the page. For the sale in progress it uses the cart tool described below. If it cannot tell which page you were on, it says so.

### Ask about the shop's figures
Ask things like *How much is the red Highland Cow, and how many do we have?*, *What is low on stock?*, *How much did we sell today?*, *How many Tadlings did we sell this month?*, *Find order 1042*, *What deals are on right now?*, *Find the customer Priya* or *Which gift cards did we sell this week?* The assistant looks at what is saved on **this till** and answers from that. It does not add anything up itself: sales totals come already added up, the same way the **Reports** page adds them. It tells you plainly when nothing matched. It also knows today's date and the time from the iPad's clock, so *yesterday*, *this week* and *this month* mean the right days.

Good to know:
- It only knows this till. The sales and refunds it can find are the latest 2000 saved here, and the totals it reports are this till's plus any imported Square history. Other tills are not included, so a total here can be lower than Reports when other tills are selling.
- A gift card's **remaining balance** is not something it can look up. Use the **Gift cards** screen for that. It can tell you which cards were sold and paid with on this till.
- Products, prices and stock come from the catalogue saved on this iPad, so stock is as of the last sync. It is not a live look at Shopify. A product that is not tracked is listed as *Not tracked*, and a draft or archived product is only found when you ask for it.
- What it is allowed to read depends on the shop's privacy rules (see **What the assistant may see** in [[settings/assistant]]). When something is hidden, it says it cannot show it. With a model that is not on the shop's own network, that means customer names, emails and phone numbers, staff names, gift card codes and how an order was paid. What was sold, the prices and the totals are still available.

### Ask how the till is doing
Ask things like *Is the till syncing?*, *Why is this not updating?*, *How many sales are waiting to upload?*, *When did the catalogue last import?* or *Is the card reader ready?* The assistant reads the same status the till already shows on **Support & diagnostics** and in **Notifications**: whether it is syncing and when it last did, how many sales are waiting to upload and whether any need a person, whether the card reader is ready, whether Shopify is connected, when the catalogue was last imported, and the latest problems in plain words. It cannot fix anything or sync for you. It can tell you which screen to open, and a **Guide me** button can point you to it.

Good to know:
- It describes the till as it was when you asked. Ask again after you tap **Sync now** to see what changed.
- Card payments and receipts are not listed, and there is no printer connection in this app to report on.
- Problems are shown as one short line each, with web addresses taken out. Emails, phone numbers, card numbers and keys in them are hidden the same way as everything else it reads.

### Ask about the drawer, the cart and cash sums
Ask things like *What should be in the drawer?*, *Which notes do we have?*, *Why won't this sale go through?*, *What change do I give for $23.45 if they hand me $50?*, *Split $100 three ways* or *What should I bank today?* The assistant reads the shared cash drawer and the cart on the till as they were when you asked, and does the sums with the till's own rules, so it never works out cash itself. It can say what the drawer should hold, which notes and coins the ledger says are in it, the change to give (from the drawer where it can), the payments of a split, and a float suggestion like the Daily float report. For the cart it lists the lines, discounts and total, any price adjustments waiting for a check, and any cart warning that must be ticked before payment.

Good to know:
- It only reads. It never opens, counts or changes the drawer, and never edits the cart.
- The ledger only knows the notes and coins that were entered, so a physical count can differ. It says so when the ledger and the expected amount disagree.
- With cash rounding on, change is worked out from the amount due rounded to the nearest 5c.
- It never shows a gift card code or who a card is for, and the cart answer holds no customer, note or payment detail.

### What it cannot do
It never changes anything: no prices, refunds, carts, stock, customers or settings. It only answers.

### If it does not answer
A red bar says what went wrong in plain words: not set up, cannot reach the model, took too long, key rejected, model not found. **Retry** appears when trying again could help. An owner also gets **Open model settings**. Everyone else is told to ask the owner or a manager.

Below your question it still gives you a list, headed *Model offline, showing search results.* The list is a plain search of the till's **screens** and **help pages** for the words you typed, with no model, so it is a list of matches and not an answer. For each screen it says what the screen is for and the taps to open it from the Checkout tab, with an **Open** button when the screen is a tab or a page that can be opened that way (a window cannot, so its taps are listed). Tap a help page to read it. It only lists things your role can use, and if nothing matches it says it could not find anything. This also works before the model is set up. Your next question tries the model first again, and the red bar goes when it answers. **Retry** replaces the list with the model's answer.
sections.deep:
### What is kept
Your messages and its replies are kept on this iPad, for you only. Each person who signs in has their own. They are not shared with other registers and are not in Backup & transfer. The newest 200 messages are kept. Tap the bin at the top to clear your own history. Nothing clears it by itself.

### What is hidden before sending
Before anything leaves the iPad, email addresses, Australian and international phone numbers, card numbers and keys or tokens are replaced with a tag such as [email address]. A line under your message says what was hidden. This happens on every model, local or remote, and it also runs again over older messages each time you ask something new. Shop data the assistant is later given goes through a stricter check first, set in **What the assistant may see** in [[settings/assistant]].

### The conversation log
Every question you send and every answer or error is also written to a log on this iPad, so the manager can see what was asked and what the model was sent. A line under the chat says so. The log is separate from your chat history: clearing your history with the bin does not touch it. It keeps what was sent after the hiding described above, so a card number you typed is not in it, and it never holds the API key. It stays on this iPad, is not shared with other registers and is not in Backup & transfer. There is no screen to read it yet. The manager's viewer, with export and clear, comes in the next patch.

If a message cannot be added to the log (the iPad is out of space, for example), you still get your answer. A red line under the chat says *This conversation could not be added to the log. Tell a manager.*

### What shop data it can see
Seven tools read the shop's data, all from what is saved on this iPad:
- **Find products**: a product or variation by name, SKU, barcode or category, with its price and stock in the same words as the Stock check tile (*In stock*, *Out of stock*, *Not tracked*, *oversold*). Ask for detail and it adds SKU, barcode, the usual price, cost, tags, categories and the deals that could apply, for up to three products.
- **Stock levels**: what is low, out of stock, oversold or not tracked, for the whole catalogue or one category, with the counts already added up. *Low* is the same as the low filter on the Inventory tab: 2 or fewer, which includes out of stock.
- **Sales report** for a period (today, yesterday, this week, last month, or two dates): orders, discounts, refunds, net sales, takings by payment method, top items and categories, cost and profit, and the sales by each staff member where names may be sent. It can also count how many of one item were sold.
- **Find orders**: the newest ten sales and refunds that match an order number, an item, a customer or some dates. Ask for detail and it gives the items, prices, deals, price adjustments and notes of up to three.
- **Deals**: the bundle deals, automatic discounts and manual discounts, what each does and whether it is running now.
- **Find customers**: by name, email or phone, with their order count and spending as last synced.
- **Gift card activity**: cards sold and payments made with a card, filtered by the last four or more characters of a code.

Every answer from these goes through the privacy check before the model sees it, and the conversation log shows what the model was given and how many items were hidden.

### What it can see about the till itself
One more tool, **app status**, reads how the till is doing, from what is saved on this iPad and in the app right now: the app version and build, the sync state and when it last finished, how many sales are waiting to upload (and how many are stuck and need a person), the oldest one waiting and up to three different error messages, whether the card reader is ready and what it says, whether Shopify is connected, whether a receipt page is set up, how many variations the catalogue holds and when it was last imported, and the last five notices about syncing, the queue, stock, the reader and general information. Refund and pass notices are left out because they name customers and staff. It does not read any sale, any card attempt, or any notice's body. Every role can use it, because Support & diagnostics is open to every role.

### What it can see about the drawer and the cart
Three tools read the cash drawer and the sale in progress from a snapshot taken when you ask (`takeCashState` in `src/lib/assistantCashIO.ts`). **Cash drawer** gives the shift, what it should hold, the ledger's notes and coins, today's takings and the last five movements, without staff names or notes. **Cash calculator** does change, split payments and a float suggestion, using `planChange`, `equalPlan`, `firstPlan` and `recommendFloat`. **Current cart** gives the priced lines, totals, price checks and the warnings set to show at Charge. A warning set to queue is only counted, because it goes on the warning list and never stops Charge. Every role can use all three, because the drawer and the cart are open to every role. On practice data the snapshot is empty and the tools say they could not read the till.

### Practice mode
The chat is switched off in practice mode, and that includes the search list. Practice mode never sends shop data out. In a training **Check**, the practice bar has an **Ask coach** button beside **Hint**. It is the assistant, but as a coach: tap it, type what you are stuck on, and it answers in a sentence or two without doing the task for you. Each question uses a hint, the same as the **Hint** button, so the bar shows the same hint and the count of hints you used goes up. The first question opens hint 1, the next hint 2, and so on. Asking it to *just tell me* does not skip ahead, because the app decides which hint is open, not the coach. When every written hint has been used, the coach says so and sends you to **Hint**, which is the only thing that highlights the answer. If you have gone off course, it points you at the card in the bar and uses no hint. If the model cannot answer, you still get the hint itself. The coach knows the course name, the goal and the hints opened so far, and nothing else: no shop data, no drawer, no cart, no settings. It can look at help pages and screens for how a feature works in general. Questions to the coach are logged for the manager, marked as practice, under your own name and not the practice cashier's. **Start again** clears the conversation and puts the hints back to the start.
sections.advanced:
### What goes to the model
Only the short rules the app gives it, then as many of the newest messages as fit in the **Context size** from the AI assistant settings (a quarter is kept free for the reply). Older messages stay on the iPad for you to scroll, but are not sent. Replies have em and en dashes replaced before they are shown.

### How the buttons work
The model asks for a button with the `show_link` tool, giving a kind (help page or screen) and an id it got from a search. The app checks the id against what your role may see, the same check the searches use, so a page or screen you cannot use gets the same answer as one that does not exist. The button is not part of the reply text: it is saved next to the reply, at most three, and it is checked again each time the chat is drawn, so if your role loses access later, the button is gone. Buttons are never sent back to the model. A button can only open a help page, a tab or a page that needs nothing else; it never opens an address on the web and never changes anything. Code: `resolveLink` and `liveLinks` in `src/lib/assistantTools.ts`, the `target` of each screen in `src/lib/assistantScreens.ts`.

### How the guide works
The model asks for the button with the `show_guide` tool, giving a screen id from `search_screens` (which marks the screens that can be guided with `can_guide`). The app checks it for your role exactly as it does for `show_link`, so a screen you cannot reach gets the same answer as one that does not exist. Each screen carries its walk: the controls to tap from the Checkout tab, read from the same graph that gives the plain words, with the words said at each tap. A screen gets no walk if any tap has no control or no words, if the control is not a real spot in the till, or if the walk goes into a window. The ring does not remember where you are: several times a second it looks at which controls of the walk are on screen and points at the last one, so tapping something else or starting part of the way along both work. A guide to a tab or a page ends when you arrive there. A guide to a view of Checkout (such as Keypad) ends when one of that view's own controls is on screen, or when you tap the last control. The ring and card are drawn on the main screen only, never inside a window. The guide changes nothing: it only points. Code: `src/lib/assistantGuide.ts` (the rules and the one active guide, tested), `src/ui/AssistantGuide.tsx` (the ring and card), `walk` of each screen in `src/lib/assistantScreens.ts`, `resolveLink` and `show_guide` in `src/lib/assistantTools.ts`.

### How the log is kept
One file for each day, in a folder inside the app that Files.app cannot see (`Library/Application Support/assistant-log/`, next to Documents and not inside it). A finished month is packed into one compressed file. The log has a size cap, 200 MB for now. When it is full the oldest files are removed to make room, a *purge* line is written saying how many events went and through which day, and sending is never blocked. Each line records who asked (name and role as they were then), the model and whether the address counted as local or remote, the scrubbed question, the reply, the messages sent (by id once the log already holds them, to keep it small), a checksum of the exact request, and how many items the scrubber hid in each category. The system prompt is kept once in `meta.json`. Code: `src/lib/assistantLog.ts` (logic, tested) and `src/lib/assistantLogIO.ts` (the folder). A failed request is logged too, as an error with the question that was about to be sent.

### The offline list
Since 0164 the list also shows **products** (price, stock, and a line for each variation) and a **low, out of stock or oversold** list when your question asks for one, for example *what is low on stock* or *red highland cows*. These use the same lookups as the model's product tools, from the catalogue on this iPad, so they work with no connection at all. The words of a question that are not part of a product name (*how many*, *do we have*, *price*, *stock*) are left out of the search; with one or two words all of them must match, and with three or more half is enough. Only active and unlisted products are listed, and nothing is shown in practice mode. The list is not stored. Only your question is, with a marker where a reply would be. Each time the chat is shown the list is searched again, for whoever is signed in then, so someone whose role has less access is never shown something they cannot use, even in an old chat. The model is never shown a question that only got a list, so it does not try to answer it later. A manager sees these in the conversation log as an *Offline search*, with the screens, help pages and products it found and why the model was not used.

### How the product and stock tools work
They are in `src/lib/assistantProducts.ts` and use the till's own rules, so the assistant cannot say *low* or *out* differently from the screen: `stockText` from `src/lib/lookup.ts` for the words, and `filterVariants`, `matchesStock` and `sortVariants` from `src/lib/inventoryView.ts` for the filters. `dealsFor` from `lookup.ts` gives the deals that could apply. A search needs every word to match the name, variation, SKU or barcode, as the Inventory search box does. When only some variations of a product match, only those are shown and there is no total for the product, so a total never covers more than it says. Product, price, stock, SKU, barcode and deal fields are *shop data* in the gate; the cost price is *costs and profit*, so it goes out only where that is allowed and is never in the summary form. Not tracked is stock `null` in the catalogue, and stock can be negative (oversold) by design.

### How the shop data tools work
Each tool is a plain function over a snapshot taken when you ask the question (`takeAssistantData` in `src/lib/assistantDataIO.ts`): this till's sales (the latest 2000), the daily totals saved here (this till's, any sales in the outbox not yet counted, and imported Square history), the customers, the deals and the catalogue names. They are handed nothing that can write, and a test freezes the snapshot to prove they do not change it. Money is returned as text such as $12.50 so a small model never reads cents. Each tool declares a field map that puts every field it can return into a privacy category, and the data gate removes or masks what the endpoint may not receive.
