A tool also never matches on something the model may not read: a customer is not found by name when names are hidden, and a gift card is not found by code when codes are hidden, because a match would tell the model who bought what. When names and emails are both hidden, a customer search returns an empty list and the privacy note, exactly as it does for a customer who does not exist. How an order was paid is treated as a payment detail and is never sent. Card details are never put in a result at all. On practice data the snapshot is empty, which is a second lock behind the practice mode block. Code: `src/lib/assistantData.ts` (the queries, tested), `src/lib/assistantDataTools.ts` (the tool definitions and field maps), `src/lib/assistantDataIO.ts` (the snapshot).

### How the screen context works
The chat screen reads the navigation and your display mode once, at the moment you send a question (`registerContext` in `src/lib/assistantContext.ts`), and the `screen_context` tool hands that snapshot back. The tool never reads the app itself and has nothing that can write. The last pages on the navigation stack are Help and the chat, so they are skipped to find the page you were on (`standingOn`), and the app graph names it (`screenOfRoute` in `src/lib/appGraph.ts`, the same route table training uses). A page the graph does not know is reported as one it cannot name, and the tab under it is not used in its place, because that would say the wrong screen. The page is looked up among the screens your role may reach, so a page your role cannot reach gets exactly the answer a page it cannot name gets. No ids are returned. Every field is *shop data* in the gate and none is personal, so nothing is hidden on any address. Windows are not reported: the list of open windows is only filled in during practice mode, where the chat is switched off. The guides still always start from the Checkout tab. The tool tells the model where you are, but the walks are not yet planned from your current screen.

### How the status tool works
`app_status` is in `src/lib/assistantStatus.ts`. `takeTillState` (`src/lib/assistantStatusIO.ts`) reads the store once when a question is sent, and `buildStatusView` turns it into a short list of plain values: the app version and build from `react-native-device-info`, `sync` and `zeller` from the store, the outbox (count, blocked items, oldest, distinct errors), the notices of kind sync, queue, stock, reader and info, and the catalogue times. The tool only returns that view, so it cannot read or write anything else. `safeLine` makes each message one short line and replaces web addresses with `[address]`, and the data gate then scrubs emails, phone numbers, card numbers and keys. Every field is *shop data* in the gate. The reader's ready state and message count as the app's own state and not as terminal details; no terminal id, card attempt, amount or reference is ever in the view. On practice data `takeTillState` returns nothing and the tool says it could not read the till. Tests: `tests/assistantstatus.test.ts`.

### How the coach works
The logic is in `src/lib/assistantCoach.ts` and the window is `src/ui/CoachSheet.tsx`, opened from `src/ui/TrainingDock.tsx` in a Check only. `planCoachAsk` decides what an ask does from the shared hint state (`src/lib/trainingHints.ts`): raise it one rung and ask the model, or answer by itself when the person is off course or every written hint is used. The coach never raises the ladder to the reveal. `buildCoachPrompt` is built from the course title and summary, the goal's title and the rungs opened so far. It is never given the goal's `reveal`, `until`, `inject`, `watch` or `taughtBy`, so it cannot give away what it does not hold, and a test checks this for every course. The model has three tools (`search_docs`, `read_doc`, `search_screens`) and at most 4 calls a question. After the model answers, `coachLeaks` compares every number in the reply with the numbers in the goal, the opened hints and the question. A reply with a number from nowhere is thrown out and the hint itself is shown. Turns made above the rung the person is on are not sent to the model and are dropped from the thread when **Start again** puts the ladder back. The thread is kept in memory only. Each question is written to the audit log with `practice: true` through `coachLogSink` in `src/lib/assistantLogIO.ts`, using `realSignIn` in `src/state/trainingSession.ts` for the real staff member and role.

### Limits of this version
The offline list looks up products and stock, but not customers or sales yet. The tools are for the help pages, the screens, the button and guide tools, the seven shop data tools above, the date and time, where you were, how the till is doing, and the cash drawer, cash sums and cart. There is no live look at Shopify, so a gift card balance and other tills' sales are out of reach. A request is written to the log after the model answers or fails, so if the app is closed in the middle of a request, that request leaves no line. Phone number hiding covers Australian numbers and numbers that start with a plus sign, so a number typed another way may not be caught. Do not type customer details you would not want sent.

pages.title: AI assistant settings
pages.summary: Point the Help assistant at a model server (Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible provider) and test the connection.
pages.lead:
Use **More ▸ Settings ▸ AI assistant** to choose the model the Help assistant will use. Only an owner can open it, or a manager when the team has no owner. When staff sign-in is off, anyone can. Other people do not see the row.

This page sets up and tests the connection. To use the assistant, see [[settings/ask-assistant]].

sections.basic:
### Set it up with Ollama on the shop PC
1. On the PC, install Ollama and download a model that supports tools.
2. Make sure the iPad and the PC are on the same Wi-Fi, and that Ollama accepts connections from the network.
3. In **Address**, type the PC's address and port with `/v1` on the end, for example `http://192.168.1.20:11434/v1`.
4. In **Model name**, type the model, for example `llama3.1:8b`. Leave **API key** empty, because Ollama does not need one.
5. Tap **Test connection**. Three checks run: the server answers, the model replies, and the model can call a tool.
6. Tap **Save**.

The first time the iPad talks to a computer on your Wi-Fi, iPadOS asks for permission to find devices on the local network. Tap **Allow**.

### Use a hosted provider instead
Type the provider's address (it ends in `/v1`), the model name it gives you, and the API key. The key is kept in the iPad's Keychain and is never shown back in full.

### What the test sends
Test connection sends a short fixed message and a fake test tool. It sends nothing from the shop: no products, customers or sales.

### If a check fails
The message says what went wrong: the server could not be reached, the request took too long, the key was not accepted, the model name was not found (it lists the names the server has), or the model does not support tools. Fix that one thing and test again.
sections.deep:
### Local or remote
Under the address, the page says whether it counts as **Local** or **Remote**. Local means this iPad, a private network address (`192.168.x.x`, `10.x.x.x`, `172.16.x.x` to `172.31.x.x`) or a name ending in `.local`. Everything else counts as remote, including an address the app cannot read.

The assistant's data rules use this (see **What the assistant may see**, below). Customer details and emails may go to a local address only, and payment details and keys never go anywhere. Below that is a three way choice. **Auto** follows the address, and is right for nearly everyone. **Local** is for a private network the app does not recognise. **Remote** is for a tunnel or proxy that forwards out of your network, even when its address looks private. If you are not sure, choose Remote: it only means less is shared with the model. When you choose Local or Remote, the page adds *(set by you)* to the line above.

### What the assistant may see
The section **What the assistant may see** lists the kinds of shop data the assistant could be given, one row each, with a three way choice:

- **Auto** follows the rules for this address. On a local address customer details, email addresses and gift card balances are sent, and gift card codes only as the last four characters. On a remote address none of those are sent. Order totals and items, cost prices and profit, and stock, sales, products and deals are sent on either.
- **Always allow** sends that kind of data even where Auto would not. On a remote address the page warns you, because it means the details leave your own network. Gift card codes are never sent whole, even here: the most that goes is the last four characters.
- **Never allow** keeps that kind of data out even where Auto would send it.

Under each row, **Right now** says what the choice comes to for this address: *Sent*, *Not sent* or *Last four characters only*. **Payment details** (card details and terminal details) and **keys and passwords** are never sent, whatever you choose, and the page shows them as fixed.

These rules are applied by the app to every result before the model sees it, so the model cannot be talked into ignoring them. If something is hidden, the model is told that it was hidden and what kind it was (for example *customer details*), never what it said, so it will say it cannot show it. Order notes and other free text are checked too: an email address or phone number in a note is hidden unless that kind of data is allowed, and card numbers and keys are always hidden. If you later change the address to a remote one, or switch a row to Never allow, earlier answers in the chat that used that kind of data are no longer sent to the model. You can still read them.

These choices decide what every lookup the assistant makes, about products, sales, orders, customers, gift cards, the settings and how the till is doing, is allowed to return.

### What the assistant can read about the settings
You and the other owners and managers can ask the assistant how the register is set up: *Is cash rounding on?*, *Who has to use a PIN?*, *Which roles can't change prices?*, *Is the screensaver on?* or *What are the card fee rates?* It reads the settings as they are and says where to change one, but it never changes one. It sees yes or no and plain values: cash rounding, smart change, the fee rates, whether a receipt page, ABN, return policy, gift card claim page or pass server is set, how many owners, managers and cashiers there are, the price adjustment limits, cart warnings, display and screensaver choices, and the options on this page. It is never shown a web address, a key, a PIN, a badge code, a staff name, the business's contact details or a logo address, only whether one is set. Cashiers are not offered this tool at all, so to them a question about settings gets the same *I couldn't find anything on that* as a question about something that does not exist. The AI assistant options on this page are in the answer only for a person who can open this page.

### Options
- **Temperature** is how adventurous the model's wording is. Low is steadier.
- **Timeout** is how long one request may take. The default is 120 seconds.
- **Context size** is how much text the model can read at once. If the provider reports it, Test connection fills it in. With Ollama, set the context size on the Ollama side too, because this connection cannot set it.
- **Tool call limit** stops a model that gets stuck calling tools in a loop. The default is 15.

### Per iPad, and in backups
These settings are for this iPad and are not shared with other registers. They are included in **Backup & transfer**, together with the key, so a restored iPad can reach the same model. See [[settings/backup]].
sections.advanced:
### How it is built
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[AssistantSettings.tsx] --> B[parseBaseUrl and classifyEndpoint in assistantConfig.ts]
  A --> C[testConnection in assistantClient.ts]
  C --> D[listModels then chat then chat with the test tool]
  A --> E[assistantKey.ts in the Keychain]
  A --> F[settings.assistant in store.ts]
```

- The settings are `settings.assistant` (type `AssistantSettings` in `src/lib/assistantConfig.ts`). `normaliseAssistant` fills defaults and clamps every value, on load and on restore.
- `pushSharedSettings` in `src/lib/sync.ts` builds its list by hand and does not include `assistant`, so nothing here syncs between registers.
- The key is stored as `pos.assistantKey` through `src/lib/assistantKey.ts`. It is not in `settings`. It is carried in the backup credentials as `assistantKey` (`src/lib/backupFile.ts`, `src/lib/backupIO.ts`).
- `src/lib/assistantClient.ts` takes a `fetch` function, so the tests run without a network. It does not stream replies. Server error text is cut short and the key is removed from it before it is shown.
- The row is shown when `canEditAdjustPerms(actingRole(...), staff)` is true. Practice mode blocks saving, Test connection and writing the key.
- iOS reaches a local address over plain http because the local networking exception (NSAllowsLocalNetworking) is set in `app.json`.

Tests: `tests/assistantconfig.test.ts`, `tests/assistantclient.test.ts`, `tests/assistantsettings.test.ts`, `tests/assistantgate.test.ts`.

### How the settings reader works
`read_settings` is in `src/lib/assistantStatus.ts`. It lists `roles: ['manager', 'owner']` on the tool, and `toolsFor(role)` in `assistantTools.ts` leaves it out of the request for anyone else, with the prompt built from the same list (`buildSystemPrompt` takes the tool names), so a cashier's request does not name it. If it is called anyway the answer is the one for a tool that does not exist. `takeTillState(role)` (`src/lib/assistantStatusIO.ts`) only builds the settings view for a manager or an owner, and `buildSettingsView` copies plain values only: it never receives or copies an address, a token, a PIN hash, a badge hash or a staff name. The AI assistant group is built only when `canEditAdjustPerms` says this person may see these settings, the same rule as the row in Settings. The tool takes one optional group (`register`, `checkout`, `receipts`, `staff` or `display`); the AI assistant group is only in the full answer. Every field is *shop data* in the gate. Tests: `tests/assistantstatus.test.ts`.

### The data gate
`src/lib/assistantGate.ts` is the one place the data rules live. `resolvePolicy(scope, toggles)` turns the endpoint class (`classifyEndpoint`) and the per category toggles (`settings.assistant.gate`) into a decision for each of nine categories: `allow`, `last4` or `deny`. Payment and secret are always `deny`, and Always allow on `gift_code` is `last4`. `applyGate(result, spec, policy)` walks a tool result.

- Every tool declares `gate` (`AssistantTool` in `assistantTools.ts`): a field map that names each field it can return and its category, or `'content'` for tools that return only help text. `runToolCall` calls `applyGate` straight after `tool.run`, before the result is cut to size, so the model and the log only ever hold the gated result.
- A field the map does not name is dropped and counted under `unknown`. An object where the map expects a single value is dropped too. Nothing is thrown.
- Every string that is kept goes through the scrubber (`assistantScrub.ts`). Emails are left alone only when `email` is `allow`, phone numbers only when `personal` is `allow`. Card numbers that pass the Luhn check and key shaped strings are always masked.
- With no policy given, `FAIL_CLOSED_POLICY` (the remote rules) applies.
- Each reply is marked with the categories its tool results held (`used` on the chat entry). `forModel` leaves out a reply, and its question, when the current policy no longer sends one of them.
- The counts of what was withheld, by category and never the items, are on each tool record and on the log event (`withheld`).

Tests: `tests/assistantgate.test.ts`. `assertNoUnknownFields` in that file is the check every data tool added later should call with realistic data.

Known to change: the data tools themselves (products, inventory, sales, customers and the rest) are later patches. See `docs/AI_ASSISTANT_PLAN.md`.

pages.title: Backup, transfer and local data
pages.summary: Export and restore settings securely, move them to another iPad, or export and delete local CSV history.
pages.lead: Use **More ▸ Settings ▸ Backup & transfer** to move settings and logins to another iPad. Use **More ▸ Settings ▸ Data** to export or delete this iPad's local CSV history; these are separate tools.

sections.basic:
### Create a backup
1. In **Backup & transfer**, enter a passphrase of at least **8 characters** in **Passphrase** and **Repeat passphrase**.
2. Tap **Export encrypted backup**, then save or share the file somewhere safe.
3. Keep the passphrase separate and safe. It is needed to open the encrypted backup.

The encrypted backup includes settings, staff, the grid layout and logins, including the AI assistant's address, model and API key (see [[settings/assistant]]). It does not include sales history or the product catalogue. Zeller reader pairing stays on the original iPad.

**Export plain JSON (not encrypted)** is available only after a warning and confirmation. The file contains Shopify and other login secrets in readable text. Prefer the encrypted backup; if you export plain JSON, protect it and delete it after importing.

### Restore on another iPad
Tap **Choose backup file…** and select the backup. For an encrypted file, enter its passphrase and tap **Decrypt & restore**. Confirm the restore. It replaces the receiving iPad's settings, grid and logins, but keeps that iPad's own register name and ID.

After restoring, open **Settings ▸ Shopify** and tap **Import from Shopify** to reload the catalogue. Pair the Zeller reader again on the receiving device.

### Export or delete CSV history
Open **Settings ▸ Data**. **Export data** asks what you want and saves it as CSV files or a spreadsheet; see [[orders/export]]. **Export raw CSV files** shares the local history files exactly as written. Every sale, refund and declined card attempt is kept on this device and the files are not auto-cleared.

**Delete local history** asks twice before erasing the CSV files from this iPad. Export first if you need them. Deleting these local files does not delete the orders in Shopify.
sections.deep:
### What is and is not transferred
The backup carries settings, staff, the Checkout grid and configured logins such as Shopify, receipt and pass-server credentials. Sales history and the imported catalogue are not in the backup; Shopify remains the source to import them again. The Zeller reader pairing, register name and register ID belong to the receiving device and are not overwritten.

An encrypted file cannot be opened without its passphrase. A plain JSON backup includes secrets and should be treated like a password file. Uploaded screensaver logos can be included in the backup; the device-specific local file path is not copied.

### Local CSV history
The CSV files are separate from Shopify orders and the backup. They stay in the app's files on this iPad until you share or delete them. Deleting the local files cannot be undone from this screen.
sections.advanced:
### Backup and restore path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Collect settings grid and credentials] --> B[Encrypt with passphrase or export plain JSON]
  B --> C[Share backup file]
  C --> D[Choose file on receiving iPad]
  D --> E[Decrypt when needed and confirm restore]
  E --> F[Keep destination register identity]
  E --> G[Import catalogue from Shopify]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Backup and Data screens | `BackupSettings`, `DataSettings` in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Collect and apply settings, logins and grid | `collectBackup`, `applyBackup` in `src/lib/backupIO.ts` |
| Validate, encrypt and decrypt backup files | `validateBackup`, `encryptBackup`, `decryptBackup` in `src/lib/backupFile.ts` |
| CSV export and deletion | `src/lib/csvStore.ts` |
| Test backup and restore rules | `tests/backup.test.ts` |

Encrypted backups use a passphrase-derived key and authenticated encryption. Plain JSON explicitly confirms before exporting because it contains credentials. Restoring merges nested settings with the receiving app's defaults and preserves its register identity.

pages.title: Hardware and the scanner test
pages.summary: Pair a Bluetooth scanner as an HID keyboard, test it in Settings and check what the scanner returns.
pages.lead: Use **More ▸ Settings ▸ Hardware** to test a Bluetooth scanner without changing the cart. Pair the scanner in the iPad's Bluetooth settings in **HID keyboard** mode first.

sections.basic:
### Test a scanner
1. Pair the Bluetooth scanner with the iPad as a keyboard in HID mode.
2. Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Hardware**.
3. Scan a barcode. The scanner test lists the last few codes it received, with how fast each one was typed in (milliseconds per character).

The test shows the raw scanned text. It does not look up an item and does not add anything to a cart. For the camera scanner, item lookup and common scan problems, see [[sales/scanners]].

### If the scan does not appear
Check that the scanner is connected to this iPad and configured as a keyboard (HID). Return to **Hardware** and scan again. If it appears in the test but not on Checkout, use the scanner guide to check the screen and input rules: [[sales/scanners]].

### The speed test
If scanned codes come in with missing or wrong characters, use **Speed test** on the same screen. Tap **Show the speed test barcode**, scan it, and the app times the scan, says which scanner speed it matches, and offers the next slower speed's barcode. The setup barcodes are on [[settings/scanner-codes]].

### Calibrate (managers and owners)
Managers and owners also see **Admin ▸ Calibrate**. Pick a speed, set the scanner to it by scanning its setup barcode, then scan the speed test barcode 3 to 12 times and tap **Save**. Do this for all four speeds. Every register then uses the same ranges. **Reset to the manual's ranges** removes the calibration.
sections.deep:
### How the HID test works
A Bluetooth HID scanner sends the barcode as keyboard input and finishes it with Return. The POS catches that text in a hidden input field; the Hardware test then shows the complete scanned value. Because this screen only records scans, it can confirm what the scanner sent without depending on a product's barcode or SKU being correct.

### How the speed is timed and shared
The hidden scan box records when its text changes. The time from the first change to the last, divided by the number of gaps between characters, is the milliseconds per character. If the iPad hands over several characters at once at the fastest speeds, the measurement reads a little slow, which is why calibrating on this iPad is better than trusting the manual's numbers. A calibrated range runs from the lowest to the highest measurement, widened by 10% (at least 0.5 ms). A calibration is refused if the speeds end up out of order. It is saved in the `pos_settings` metaobject under the handle `scanner`, so it needs no new setup, and the registers pick it up when they next poll. If Shopify cannot be reached it is kept on this register and sent later.
sections.advanced:
### Test input path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Pair scanner as HID keyboard] --> B[Open Hardware test]
  B --> C[Scanner types code and Return]
  C --> D[Show raw code in recent scans]
  D --> E[Cart and catalogue stay unchanged]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Hardware test UI, recent scan list, speed test and Calibrate menu | `HardwareTest`, `CalibrateSheet` in `src/screens/ScannerSpeed.tsx` |
| Bluetooth HID input | `HidScanner` in `src/screens/Scanner.tsx` |
| Scan activity and input completion | `noteActivity` in `src/lib/idle.ts`, submit handler in `src/screens/Scanner.tsx` |
| Item/pass/gift-card scan handling | `src/screens/Scanner.tsx`, `src/lib/lookup.ts` |
| Timing a scan, ranges, saving rules | `noteChange`, `measure`, `rangeFromSamples`, `calibrationProblems`, `canCalibrate` in `src/lib/scanSpeed.ts` |
| Share the calibration between registers | `saveScannerCalibration`, `pushScannerCalibration` in `src/lib/sync.ts` (pulled in the same poll as the other shared settings) |
| Scanner guide | `help/sales/scanners.md` |

The Hardware test keeps the most recent eight scans in memory while it is open. It does not save those scan values to the catalogue or sales history.

pages.title: Payment settings
pages.summary: Set cash rounding, Smart change and estimated card fee rates, and open Zeller reader setup.
pages.lead: Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Payments** to choose cash rounding, Smart change and the fee rates used in POS estimates. Reader setup is in **Support & diagnostics**.

sections.basic:
### Cash rounding
**Cash rounding (5c)** rounds the amount due in cash to the nearest five cents. It applies to the cash amount only; card payments are not rounded by this setting. The setting is on by default.

### Smart change
Turn on **Smart change** to choose notes and coins that leave the drawer better stocked for later sales. It applies to this register only. For how the choice is calculated, see [[cash/smart-change]].

### Card fee rates and the terminal
Set **Card-present fee %** and **Keyed / card-not-present fee %** to match the rates you use. They are estimates for reports; the Zeller SDK does not return the actual fee. A card refund does not return the original fee.

To pair or check the reader, tap **Reader & pairing**. In **Support & diagnostics**, use **Setup (pair terminal)**. Card payments need a network connection and a paired terminal. The **Automatic cash tender machine** option is still under construction and disabled; cash notes and coins are handled by hand.
sections.deep:
### What each choice affects
- Cash rounding applies to the amount due on a cash tender, not card or gift-card amounts.
- Smart change is a per-register preference and works with the drawer's note-and-coin counts and sales history.
- Card fee rates are stored as shared settings and are used to estimate fees. Changing a rate does not change the amount charged by Zeller.
- Reader pairing is device-specific. If you reinstall the app, pair the terminal again.

The default estimates are **1.4%** for card-present and **1.7%** for keyed/card-not-present. Adjust them if your actual rate differs.
sections.advanced:
### Payment settings and reader path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Choose rounding or fee estimates] --> B[Save payment settings]
  C[Open Reader and pairing] --> D[Support and diagnostics]
  D --> E[Setup pair terminal]
  E --> F[Check reader before taking card payment]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Payments section | `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Default fee rates and rate selection | `DEFAULT_FEES`, `feeRate` in `src/lib/fees.ts` |
| Cash rounding | `cashRounding` in `src/lib/cashSale.ts` |
| Reader pairing and test purchase controls | `src/screens/Diagnostics.tsx` |
| Zeller payment request and results | `src/lib/zeller.ts`, `src/screens/Pay.tsx` |

The fee estimates are recorded with sales for reporting; they are not a quote from the terminal. The Settings footer explains that actual card fees are not provided by the Zeller SDK.

pages.title: Receipt settings
pages.summary: Configure the receipt page, business details, ABN, return policy and GST tax invoices.
pages.lead: Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Receipts** to add your business details to receipts and connect the receipt page that customers open from a QR code or link.

sections.basic:
### Enter business details
Fill in **Business / trading name**, **ABN**, **Address**, **Phone**, **Email** and **Website** as needed. Add a **Return policy (optional)** if you want it printed. When the business name is blank, the receipt uses your Shopify shop name.

These details are copied into each receipt when it is made. Changing them later does not rewrite receipts that have already been issued.

### Connect and test the receipt page
Enter the **Receipt server URL** and **Receipt server secret (RECEIPT_SECRET)** supplied for your receipt server. Tap **Send test receipt** to upload a sample and open its page. The server must be deployed and configured before the link can work.

When a receipt page is configured, the customer can scan a QR or open a link to see the receipt and download it. For the customer-facing Receipt sheet and receipt page, see [[pay/receipts]].

### GST tax invoices
Turn on **Registered for GST** only if your business is registered. Receipts are then titled **Tax invoice** and show the GST included in the total. Prices are treated as GST-inclusive; gift-card lines are excluded from the GST calculation.
sections.deep:
### What appears on the receipt
The seller name, ABN and contact details, return policy, receipt and order information, items, payments and totals are captured in the receipt snapshot. The GST amount is calculated as one-eleventh of the GST-inclusive total for non-gift-card lines. The Receipt server renders the uploaded snapshot as a page with PDF and image download.

Use the test button to check that the URL and server secret work together. If it fails, confirm the Worker is deployed and that the URL and `RECEIPT_SECRET` match its configuration.
sections.advanced:
### Receipt publishing path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Enter receipt server URL and secret] --> B[Make sample receipt]
  B --> C[Upload snapshot to receipt server]
  C --> D[Open customer receipt page]
  E[Save seller and GST details] --> F[Copy details into each new receipt]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Receipt settings form and test upload | `ReceiptSettings` in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Receipt profile and GST calculation | `ReceiptProfile`, `gstIncluded`, `buildReceiptDoc` in `src/lib/receiptDoc.ts` |
| Upload a sample receipt | `uploadSampleReceipt` in `src/lib/receiptSync.ts` |
| Save the server secret | `getReceiptSecret`, `setReceiptSecret` in `src/lib/shopify/client.ts` |
| Receipt page and customer options | `help/pay/receipts.md` |

The receipt server URL is a setting; the receipt secret is stored in the iOS Keychain on this device. The POS snapshots business details into each new receipt so old receipts keep the details they were issued with.

pages.title: Scanner setup barcodes
pages.summary: The setup barcodes for the POS-mate Bluetooth scanner (pairing, sound, vibration, sleep, scan mode and speed), drawn on screen so you can scan them.
pages.lead: The scanner is changed by scanning special setup barcodes. This page shows them on the screen, so you do not need the paper manual. Scan the barcode **from the iPad's screen** with the scanner you want to change.

sections.basic:
### How to use it
1. Scroll to the setting you want to change below.
2. Tap its barcode. The whole screen goes white and shows only that barcode and a line saying what it does.
3. Point the scanner at the barcode and scan it. The scanner beeps or buzzes to say it took the setting.
4. Tap anywhere to go back.

Turn the screen brightness up if the scanner struggles to read it.

### What each group does
- **Pairing.** Scan **Pairing mode**, then pair the scanner in the iPad's Settings ▸ Bluetooth so it works as a keyboard (HID).
- **Vibration** and **Volume.** How the scanner tells you a scan worked.
- **Sleep.** How long it waits, unused, before sleeping. **Never sleep** drains the battery faster.
- **Scanning mode.** **Manual** scans only while you press the trigger. **Auto** scans by itself when a barcode is held in front of it.
- **Data entry speed.** How fast the scanner types the code into the iPad.

Settings marked **(default)** are how the scanner leaves the factory.

### If barcodes come in wrong
Characters missing or jumbled when you scan an item usually mean the scanner is typing faster than the iPad can take it. Scan **Medium speed**, then try again. Still wrong? Try **Slow speed**, then **Super slow speed**. To find the right one without guessing, see the speed test below.
sections.deep:
### The speed test
The app times it for you: open Settings ▸ **Hardware**, tap **Show the speed test barcode** and scan it (see [[settings/hardware]]). The scanner types `HID_SCANNER_SPEED_TEST` and then presses Return. The app divides the time from first to last character by the number of gaps and picks the nearest speed. The manual's ranges, used until a manager or owner calibrates, are:

| Setting | Time between characters |
|---|---|
| Fast | 3 to 6 ms |
| Medium | 17 to 21 ms |
| Slow | 42 to 46 ms |
| Super slow | 150 to 152 ms |

If a result is between two rows, the nearer one wins, and if two are equally near, the one whose middle is closer. A manager or owner can replace these ranges with measured ones in **Hardware ▸ Admin ▸ Calibrate**, and every register shares them. The speeds are named by how long a whole code takes: Fast is about 6 codes a second, Medium about 1 a second, Slow about 1.5 seconds a code and Super slow about 6 seconds a code.

### Why scanning a screen works
Each setup barcode is an ordinary Code 128 barcode whose text is a command the scanner understands, such as `%%SpecCode77`. The scanner reads the text and changes its own setting instead of typing it. Because the POS draws the barcode itself from that text, nothing needs printing.
sections.advanced:
### From tap to full screen
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Help page settings/scanner-codes] --> B[ScannerCodes lists SCANNER_CODE_GROUPS]
  B --> C[Barcode128 draws each text with code128Path]
  C -->|tap a card| D[BarcodeFullScreen Modal]
  D -->|tap anywhere| B
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| The codes (label, text, what it does, default) | `SCANNER_CODE_GROUPS` in `src/lib/scannerCodes.ts` |
| Picking a speed from a measured time | `speedForInterval`, `SPEED_TABLE`, `DEFAULT_SPEED_RANGES` in `src/lib/scannerCodes.ts` |
| Timing, calibration and sharing | `src/lib/scanSpeed.ts`, `src/screens/ScannerSpeed.tsx`, `saveScannerCalibration` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| The list and the full-screen view | `ScannerCodes`, `BarcodeFullScreen` in `src/screens/ScannerCodes.tsx` |
| Drawing a barcode from text | `code128Path` in `src/lib/code128.ts`, `Barcode128` in `src/ui/Barcode128.tsx` |
| The shortcut buttons (big one on Checkout help) | `SCANNER_SHORTCUT` in `src/screens/Help.tsx` |
| Tests | `tests/scannercodes.test.ts`, `tests/scanspeed.test.ts` |

To add or fix a code, edit its `text` in `SCANNER_CODE_GROUPS`. Only printable ASCII works (Code 128 subset B); `tests/scannercodes.test.ts` fails on anything else or on a repeated id or text.

### Reading the code for a fault
- **The scanner does not react.** The text differs from the manual by a character, or the screen is too dim. Compare `text` with the manual.
- **A code will not draw.** `code128Modules` throws on characters outside ASCII 32 to 126; the test catches this.

pages.title: Connecting Shopify
pages.summary: Enter the shop domain and app credentials, test the connection, choose a location and import the catalogue.
pages.lead: Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Shopify** to connect the register to a Shopify store, choose the stock location and import its catalogue.

sections.basic:
### Connect a shop
1. Enter the **Store domain**, **Client ID (Dev Dashboard app)** and **Client secret**.
2. Tap **Save & test connection**. The register checks the credentials with Shopify and shows the shop name and reported scopes if successful.
3. Choose a **Location (stock & orders)** if more than one active location is available.
4. Tap **Import from Shopify** to load variants, collections, customers and discounts.

The domain can be entered as `yourshop.myshopify.com`; the screen normalises it. The Client ID and Client secret are from your Shopify Dev Dashboard app. They are stored in the iOS Keychain on this iPad, not shared with the other registers.

### Shared storage and disconnecting
If you use multiple registers, tap **Set up shared storage (metaobjects)** to prepare the Shopify metaobjects used for shared POS data. **Disconnect** removes the Shopify credentials from this iPad; the existing local catalogue remains until you import again.
sections.deep:
### Which location is used
The selected active Shopify location is used for stock and orders. When Shopify reports a single active location and none has been saved yet, the register selects it automatically. With multiple active locations, choose the one this register should use.

The import button refreshes product variants, collections, customers and discounts from Shopify. The connected shop name and local catalogue counts appear on the Shopify settings screen.

### If the connection fails
Check the shop domain and the Client ID and Client secret for the Dev Dashboard app, then use **Save & test connection** again. A successful connection displays a message naming the shop. If it connects but the import fails, check the message shown by **Import from Shopify** and retry when Shopify is available.
sections.advanced:
### Connection and import path
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Enter shop domain and app credentials] --> B[Save credentials in iOS Keychain]
  B --> C[Request Shopify access token]
  C --> D[Fetch shop and active locations]
  D --> E[Choose location for stock and orders]
  E --> F[Import variants collections customers and discounts]
  E --> G[Set up shared storage when using multiple registers]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Connection form and import controls | `ShopifySettings` in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Store-domain cleanup and secure credentials | `normaliseDomain`, `saveCreds` in `src/lib/shopify/client.ts` |
| Access token and Admin GraphQL requests | `getToken`, `gql` in `src/lib/shopify/client.ts` |
| Shop name and active locations | `fetchShop` in `src/lib/shopify/catalogue.ts` |
| Bulk catalogue import | `importFromShopify` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |
| Shared storage definitions | `ensureDefinitions` in `src/lib/shopify/metaobjects.ts` |

The access token is created by the app and refreshed automatically; you do not enter a token in Settings. Credentials and token are kept in the iOS Keychain on this device.

For a completed sale that is queued or blocked from uploading, see [[fix/offline-sync]].

pages.title: Theme, tiles and accent
pages.summary: Choose the Aiden’s 3D Printing brand, Light, Dark or System appearance, adjust tile size, add glass-style surfaces, and spotlight scanned or tapped items.
pages.lead: Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Theme** to change this register's appearance, Checkout tile size, accent colour and optional item spotlight.

sections.basic:
### Choose an appearance
Select **Aiden’s brand**, **Light**, **Dark** or **System**. The brand theme uses the shop's plum background, peach text and peach primary buttons. **System** follows the iPad's appearance setting.

Turn on **Glass surfaces** for translucent blurred cards and buttons. This is a cross-platform React Native glass-style treatment, not Apple's exact iOS 26 Liquid Glass material.

### Change tile size and accent
Choose **Small**, **Medium** or **Large** under **Tile size**. Tap an accent swatch to change the app's highlight colour; **Default** uses the selected theme's accent.

### Spotlight added items
In **Item spotlight**, independently turn on **Show item name** and **Show item image**. A short, large confirmation appears after an item is added by scan or tap; tap it to dismiss early. Both switches are off by default.

The register's theme, tile size and accent update immediately. A staff member's personal display preferences, set in **More ▸ Staff**, override these defaults only while that person is signed in.
sections.deep:
### Appearance does not change the grid
Theme changes colours and the general appearance. Tile size changes how large Checkout tiles appear, not which items or categories are on the grid. To edit the grid itself, see [[sales/grid]]. An item spotlight is only a visual confirmation and does not change the cart, scan result or item quantity.

Register defaults are local to this iPad. Staff-specific appearance, accent and tile-size overrides are saved with the shared staff record and follow that person to other registers.
sections.advanced:
### Theme settings
| Setting | Values | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Theme | `brand`, `light`, `dark`, `system` | `src/state/store.ts`, `src/screens/Settings.tsx`, `src/ui/theme.tsx` |
| Tile size | `S`, `M`, `L` | `src/state/store.ts`, `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Accent | Default, brand peach, plum, blue, green, red, purple or orange | `src/screens/Settings.tsx`, `src/ui/theme.tsx` |
| Item spotlight | `itemSpotlight.name`, `itemSpotlight.image` | `src/state/store.ts`, `src/screens/Checkout.tsx` |
| Glass surfaces | `glassSurfaces` | `src/state/store.ts`, `src/ui/kit.tsx` |
| Per-staff overrides | `StaffMember.preferences` | `src/lib/types.ts`, `src/screens/Staff.tsx`, `src/ui/theme.tsx`, `src/screens/Tiles.tsx` |

The item spotlight and register appearance are local settings. Personal staff appearance and tile size are stored on the shared staff record; they do not alter role permissions.

pages.title: Staff and roles
pages.summary: Add team members, set unique PINs and roles, require sign-in, and manage each person's display settings and pass.
pages.lead: Use **More ▸ Staff** to add the people who use the register, choose their role and set whether the till asks them to sign in. Each person can also have a cashier pass, display mode, appearance, accent colour and tile size.

sections.basic:
### Add a staff member
1. Tap **Add staff member**.
2. Enter their name and a unique PIN of **4-6 digits**.
3. Choose **Cashier**, **Manager** or **Owner**, then tap **Add**.

PINs must not be shared between staff members. The app stores each PIN as a salted hash and shares the staff list with your other registers.

### Require sign-in
Turn on **Require PIN to use the register** to show the sign-in screen when the register is locked. Add at least one staff member first. To sign in, enter the PIN or scan that person's cashier pass.

You can switch staff from the **Switch staff** sheet without locking the register first. The cart stays as it is. The register will not switch people while a card payment is in progress.

### Change or remove someone
Tap a person's row to open their settings. Choose their display mode, manage their cashier pass, or remove them. Removing someone makes their PIN and pass stop working.

For issuing, printing or cancelling a pass, see [[staff/passes]]. For per-person screen layout and appearance, see [[staff/modes]].
For interactive practice modules, see [[staff/training]].
sections.deep:
### What roles control
- **Cashier** accounts do not see **Reports**, **Staff** or **Settings** while staff sign-in is required.
- **Manager** and **Owner** accounts can see those More menu entries.
- Display modes can hide menu entries, but never add access that a role does not have.
- Without staff sign-in enabled, the till acts as the owner for role-gated functions.

The Staff screen also has role switches for who may set item, line and whole-order price adjustments. Owners cannot be restricted. Managers or owners can change those switches; a manager can do so when the team has no owner account.

### Staff settings are shared
PIN hashes, roles, passes, display modes and personal appearance preferences travel with the shared staff settings. A pass's scannable code is kept only on the iPad that issued it; other registers can recognise it from its hash but cannot reprint its code.
sections.advanced:
### Staff and sign-in flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Add staff name PIN and role] --> B[Store salted PIN hash in staff settings]
  B --> C[Require PIN on register]
  C --> D[Sign in by PIN or cashier pass]
  D --> E[Apply that person's role and display mode]
  E --> F[Share staff settings with other registers]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Add/remove staff and select role | `src/screens/Staff.tsx` |
| PIN hashing and verification | `hashPin`, `verifyPin` in `src/lib/pin.ts` |
| Sign-in, switching and register locking | `src/lib/staffAuth.ts` |
| Role-gated More entries | `visibleMoreRows` in `src/lib/uiMode.ts`, `src/screens/More.tsx` |
| Price-adjustment role rules | `src/lib/adjustPerms.ts` |
| Staff record | `StaffMember` in `src/lib/types.ts` |
| Shared staff settings | `pushSharedSettings` in `src/lib/sync.ts` |

Changing staff or sign-in settings updates the local settings immediately. If upload fails, the register keeps the change pending and retries while the app is open; other online registers receive it on their next poll after the upload succeeds.

pages.title: Guided checkout
pages.summary: Take a sale through Items, Discount, Check and Pay, one question at a time; add a customer from More options.
pages.lead: Guided checkout gives the cashier one step at a time: **Items**, **Discount**, **Check** and **Pay**. It is used by **Minimal** mode and can be switched on for **Custom** mode. Adding a customer is optional and does not interrupt the default flow.

sections.basic:
### Take a sale through the steps
1. **Items**: tap or scan the products. Add at least one item before pressing **Next**.
2. **Discount**: deals are applied automatically. Add a voucher or special price if needed, or tap **No, carry on**.
3. **Check**: review the items and total with the customer. Tap an item to change or remove it, then tap **Looks right**.
4. **Pay**: tap **Take payment**. Choose card, cash, gift card or a mix on the usual payment screen.

The progress bar shows which step you are on. Use **Back** to return to an earlier step.

### More options
Tap **More options** at the top to add or change a customer, add a custom amount, sell a gift card, check whether the drawer can make change, save or open a saved cart, or start again. Starting again clears the cart after confirmation.
sections.deep:
### The steps are prompts, not new sale rules
Guided checkout uses the same cart, prices, discounts, customer and payment flows as the regular Checkout screen. It does not change how a sale is calculated or recorded.

The Discount step is optional. Customer selection is available from **More options**; Custom mode can enable a separate Customer step. A new empty cart returns to **Items**. If a sale has already taken a part payment, the flow resumes at **Pay**; the part-paid sale cannot be edited until payment is finished.

### Checks before payment
The **Check** step shows the cart and any bundle combinations that need a customer check. If the cart has a price adjustment requiring confirmation, that review appears before the payment screen. The cashier still gets the deal even when a bundle is not a recommended pair.
sections.advanced:
### Flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Items add one or more] --> B[Discount optional]
  B --> C[Check items prices and deals]
  C --> D[Review price adjustments if needed]
  D --> E[Pay on the normal payment screen]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Guided screen and More options | `src/screens/GuidedCheckout.tsx` |
| Step order, progress and advance rules | `STEPS`, `canAdvance`, `settle` in `src/lib/guidedFlow.ts` |
| Select guided checkout for Minimal or Custom | `guided` in `src/lib/uiMode.ts`, `src/ui/uiProfile.tsx` |
| Guided screen navigation | `src/ui/nav.tsx` |
| Tests | `tests/guidedflow.test.ts` |

When a part payment exists, the cart is locked for editing and the guided flow settles directly on Pay so the cashier can finish the remaining balance.

pages.title: Display modes
pages.summary: Set each staff member’s Standard, Simple, Minimal or Custom mode plus their personal theme, accent and tile size.
pages.lead: Each staff member has a display mode and personal appearance preferences, set from their row in **More ▸ Staff**. These change how the POS looks for them, not their role permissions.

sections.basic:
### Choose a mode
- **Standard** shows the full app in its usual layout.
- **Simple** keeps the same features, with plain-English explanations in the More menu.
- **Minimal** uses fewer tabs and More entries, and asks one checkout question at a time.
- **Custom** lets you choose text size, tabs, each More entry, explanations and guided checkout separately.

Tap the staff member's row in Staff, select a mode under **Display mode**, then close the sheet. Each person's choice follows their staff record to the other registers.

### Custom choices
In **Custom**, choose **Normal**, **Large** or **Extra large** text; turn plain-English lines under More entries on or off; choose tab and More-menu presets, then override each tab and More entry individually; and turn **Guided steps** on or off. When guided steps are on, a separate switch can add the optional Customer step. Checkout and More tabs stay visible.

See [[staff/guided-checkout]] for what happens in that flow.

### Personal appearance
Under **Personal display preferences**, choose **Register** to inherit the current iPad's setting, or choose **Brand**, **Light**, **Dark** or **System**. Personal tile size and accent can also override the register defaults. These choices follow the staff member to other registers.
sections.deep:
### Tabs and More entries
- **All** tabs shows Checkout, Inventory, Transactions, Notifications and More.
- **No alerts** removes only the Notifications tab.
- **Basic** shows Checkout, Transactions and More.
- **All** More entries means everything the person's role allows. **Everyday** adds Items and Customers to the essential entries. **Essentials** keeps Orders, Saved carts, Gift cards, Cash drawer, Support & diagnostics, Help and Lock register, subject to role access.

Cashiers do not get manager-only entries such as Reports, Staff and Settings when staff sign-in is required. A display mode cannot grant them those entries. Checkout and More stay available so the person can do their job and get back to other parts of the app.

### The sole-admin safeguard
If the only Manager or Owner selects a mode that hides Staff or Settings, the POS shows those entries anyway. This prevents the only administrator from losing the controls needed to change the mode back.

Changing to **Custom** starts from the mode the person was using, so its text size and menu choices carry over until you change them.
sections.advanced:
### Mode resolution
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Read the staff member display mode] --> B[Resolve text tabs More and guided choices]
  B --> C[Limit More entries by staff role]
  C --> D{Only manager or owner}
  D -->|yes| E[Keep Staff and Settings visible]
  D -->|no| F[Show the resolved menus]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Mode data, presets and resolution | `src/lib/uiMode.ts` |
| Edit a staff member's mode | `src/screens/Staff.tsx` |
| Apply text sizing and tab profile | `src/ui/uiProfile.tsx` |
| Role and mode filtering in More | `visibleMoreRows` in `src/lib/uiMode.ts`, `src/screens/More.tsx` |
| Read a staff member's current mode | `src/ui/uiProfile.tsx` |
| Apply personal theme and accent | `src/ui/theme.tsx` |
| Apply personal Checkout tile size | `src/screens/Tiles.tsx` |

The modes are display preferences, not security roles. The role check is applied separately after a mode chooses which More entries to show.

pages.title: Cashier passes and signing in
pages.summary: Issue a cashier pass, print or share it, add it to Apple Wallet, and use it to sign in or switch staff.
pages.lead: A cashier pass is a scannable alternative to typing a staff member's PIN. Issue it from **More ▸ Staff**, then print it, save or share a PDF, or send it to Apple Wallet.

sections.basic:
### Issue and use a pass
1. In **More ▸ Staff**, tap the person and choose **Cashier pass**.
2. Tap **Issue pass**. Choose **QR code** or **Code 128** for a standard shop barcode scanner.
3. Print the pass, save/share the PDF, or send it to Apple Wallet.
4. On the sign-in screen or **Switch staff** sheet, scan the pass with a Bluetooth scanner. You can also tap **Scan pass** to use the camera.

Most Bluetooth scanners and the camera can read the QR code. Choose Code 128 if your scanner only reads standard shop barcodes. A PIN remains available as another way to sign in.

### Replace or cancel a pass
**Replace pass** creates a new code and immediately disables the old one. Any printed copy or Wallet pass with the old code must be replaced. **Cancel pass** disables it; the staff member can still sign in with their PIN.

### Apple Wallet
Sending to Apple Wallet needs the pass server link and secret configured in **Settings ▸ Gift cards**. The app creates the Wallet pass, then opens the iPad's share sheet so you can send it to the staff member's iPhone. They tap **Add** there.
sections.deep:
### If this iPad no longer has the code
The pass code is saved only on the iPad that issued it. The shared staff list contains a hash, which lets other registers verify scans but cannot recover or print the original code. If the issuing iPad has lost its saved copy, choose **Replace pass** on a register with the staff list; the old code will stop working and the new code can be printed or sent from that iPad.

Scanning a pass signs the person in or takes over from the currently signed-in staff member. The cart stays in place. Switching is blocked while a card payment is waiting on the reader; finish the payment first.
sections.advanced:
### Pass lifecycle
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Issue random pass code] --> B[Share salted code hash with staff settings]
  A --> C[Keep recoverable code on issuing iPad]
  C --> D[Print PDF or request Apple Wallet pass]
  E[Scan code] --> F[Match code against staff hash]
  G[Replace or cancel] --> H[Old code no longer matches]
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Issue, replace, cancel, print and share | `StaffPassSheet` in `src/screens/StaffPass.tsx` |
| Hash and match pass codes | `src/lib/badge.ts` |
| Keep the issuing iPad's copy | `src/lib/badgeStore.ts` |
| PIN/pass sign-in and switching | `src/lib/staffAuth.ts` |
| Camera and HID scanners | `CameraScanner`, `HidScanner` in `src/screens/Scanner.tsx` |
| Create an Apple Wallet pass | `requestStaffPass` in `src/lib/passUrl.ts` |

Wallet pass creation requires the separately configured pass server. Printing and PDF sharing use the iPad's print/share interfaces; those options do not require Wallet setup.

pages.title: Screensaver and keep-awake
pages.summary: Keep the iPad awake or show a branded idle screen, with a shorter wait when the register is logged out.
pages.lead: Open **More ▸ Settings ▸ Screensaver & display** to stop the iPad sleeping or show a logo screen when the register is idle. Aiden’s 3D Printing logo and plum background are supplied as defaults; you can replace the logo or colour. These choices are for this iPad, not a staff member's display mode.

sections.basic:
### Keep the iPad awake
Turn on **Keep iPad awake** to stop iOS from auto-locking or dimming while the POS is open. This is separate from the Screensaver switch. The app recommends leaving it on for a till and keeping the iPad plugged in.

### Show an idle screen
Turn on **Screensaver**, then choose **Show after** 1, 2, 5, 10 or 30 minutes. It shows a logo on a background colour; if there is no usable logo, it shows the shop name or **Point of sale**.

Tap the screen once to wake it. If the register was locked, waking the screen does not sign anyone in; use the PIN or cashier pass on the sign-in screen.

### Set a logo
Use **Logo link (https)** for a secure image URL, or tap **Upload an image from Files…**. PNG and JPG are supported; SVG files are not. An uploaded logo is stored on this iPad. You can choose a background swatch or enter a three- or six-digit hex colour, then tap **Preview full screen**.
sections.deep:
### Logged-out timing and other options
- **Show when logged out** uses a shorter wait on the PIN screen. Choose **Logged-out wait** of 5, 15, 30 or 60 seconds.
- **Slowly move the logo** drifts the image around the screen. **Show the time** adds a clock.
- When the register is logged out and the shorter wait is enabled, the screensaver uses the shorter of the logged-out wait and normal idle time.
- It never covers the screen while a card payment is waiting on the reader.

The bar along the top of the screen (time, shop, reader and sync chips, battery) stays on screen while the screensaver shows, in the screensaver's colours. Touching it wakes the screen like touching anywhere else.

The idle timer resets when someone touches the app, types or scans. The screensaver and Keep iPad awake settings belong to this device; they do not follow the staff member to another register.
sections.advanced:
### Idle screen rules
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Check screensaver enabled and time idle] --> B{Card payment waiting}
  B -->|yes| C[Keep the POS visible]
  B -->|no| D{Logged out and short wait enabled}
  D -->|yes| E[Use shorter of waits]
  D -->|no| F[Use normal idle wait]
  E --> G[Show screensaver when wait is reached]
  F --> G
```

| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Screensaver timing and UI | `src/ui/Screensaver.tsx` |
| The bar along the top, shown in the app and over the screensaver | `AppStatusBar` in `src/ui/AppStatusBar.tsx` |
| Idle timer | `idleMs`, `noteActivity` in `src/lib/idle.ts` |
| Show timing, colours and logo source | `shouldShowScreensaver`, `normaliseHex`, `logoSource` in `src/lib/screensaver.ts` |
| Screensaver settings panel | `DisplaySettings` in `src/screens/Settings.tsx` |
| Per-device settings default | `screensaver` in `src/state/store.ts` |
| Tests | `tests/screensaver.test.ts` |

The Screensaver switch is off by default. **Keep iPad awake** is on by default. A card payment waiting on the reader suppresses the screensaver even when the idle time has elapsed.

pages.title: Training mode
pages.summary: Learn app tasks through animated explanations, a process walkthrough, a spotlighted real interface and safe practice.
pages.lead: Open **More → Training** to learn a POS task. Courses can be started in any order.

sections.basic:
### How a course works
Each course has six parts:
1. **Info** is an animated visual explanation of what the task is for and when you need it. Pictures build up one step at a time, in the same style as Show, and you move on with **Next**.
2. **Show** is an animated demonstration of the whole job, drawn as a simplified copy of the till. The picture zooms in on a control, a pointer taps it, the screen responds, and a note points out what changed. You watch at your own pace: **Next** goes on, **Back** returns, **Replay** plays the current step again. Nothing moves on until you say, and you do not have to do anything yourself.
3. **Guide** opens the real POS interface with practice data. The rest of the screen dims while a bright ring and a short prompt point to the relevant control. Tap the highlighted controls or Next when a step is informational.
4. **Check 1** asks you to complete the task without the arrows, with practice data.
5. **Check 2** repeats the task with a realistic customer-side problem to recover from.
6. **Done** recaps what you can do and marks the course complete.

In the Guide and the Checks, if you wander off the path (a wrong item, a discount you did not need, the wrong screen, a window you did not need) the app says what happened, rings the control that puts it right and points at it. In the Guide the dimming lifts while you are off course, so you can tap whatever puts it right. If you have not finished the course that teaches the fix, the card also lists the steps and names the course. If you have, tap the small **?** on the card (or **Hint**) for the steps. If it cannot be undone with a tap, or you are still stuck, tap **Start this part again**; **Start again** on the bar does the same at any time. Tap **Hint** for a pointer. Each hint appears in a small card at the top of the screen ("Hint 2 of 4") and in the bar at the bottom, and pulses once so you can see it arrived. On the main screen the card fades after a few seconds and the bar keeps the text; inside a window it stays until you tap its **x**. Each hint becomes more specific; after the last hint, the app highlights the answer. If you tap Hint again after that, the card pulses again so you know the tap was heard. Pages in Training slide in as the old one drifts away, and starting or leaving practice fades through the page colour instead of cutting. Training uses a separate practice register state. Your ticks are always saved under you, even while the practice till is signed in as Casey or Morgan. Your live cart and sales are restored when you leave; practice changes are not saved, sent to Shopify, or charged to the reader.

The moving cursor shows how to do each thing: a tap, a double or triple tap, a press and hold, a swipe or a scroll. In the Guide only the ringed spot works. Everything else is dimmed and cannot be tapped, and a swipe step does not let a tap open the line underneath. If you open a window while fixing a mistake, the card talks about that window (for example the minus button) instead of telling you to close it.

### Courses so far
- **How training works**: a five minute tour of the six parts.
- **Sign in, lock and switch staff**: sign in with a PIN or a cashier pass, hand the till to a colleague from the grid, and lock it when you step away. Practice uses two practice people, **Casey** (a cashier, PIN 1234) and **Morgan** (a manager, PIN 2468, with a cashier pass). They exist only inside practice. When a step asks you to scan a pass, a drawn practice pass appears with a **Scan this pass** button, because a camera cannot scan a pass that is not real.

- **Build a cart**: add items by tapping tiles, add more of the same, and take an item out by swiping its line to the left and tapping Remove.
- **Customers and notes**: attach a customer by picking or searching, create one who is not on the list (made on this iPad only in practice), put a note on a line with Done, and take the customer off with the small x.
- **Take cash and give change**: tap the notes and coins the customer hands over, fix a slip with Undo, read Short, Exact or Change, give the change the screen shows, and handle cash rounding and a drawer that cannot make change. Practice uses its own drawer, never your real ledger.
- **Change a price**: change the price of one item (one unit, or all of it in the cart), one whole line, or the whole order for this sale only, take each off again, give a reason, and check the adjustments before payment, including a price that changed after you set it.
- **Scan items**: open the camera, scan items into the cart, read the green and red messages, add an item by hand when its label will not read, and send a customer's gift card to Charge. Practice uses a window of drawn barcodes in place of the camera.

More courses are added one at a time, most important first.

### Progress
Completion and stage progress are saved on this device for the signed-in staff member, or shared on the device when nobody is signed in. You can revisit completed stages or repeat a course.
sections.deep: Info and Show are each a list of steps over a few mock screens or diagrams. Each step can zoom the camera, move a pointer to tap a control, change what is on screen, and settle with a ring and a note. Course scenes, spotlight targets, Guide steps, Checks, recovery injections and hint ladders are declared separately from the shared runner. The Guide and Checks swap in fixture products, customers, cart, drawer and settings while the actual Checkout screens remain mounted. A guard blocks app persistence, CSV writes, Shopify calls and receipt uploads; card payments use a pretend terminal. The original app state is restored on exit.
sections.advanced:
| Job | Where |
|---|---|
| Course definitions and authoring rules | `src/training/modules/`, `src/training/README.md` |
| Course schema and validation | `src/lib/trainingModule.ts` |
| Course runner | `src/screens/TrainingRun.tsx` |
| Info and Show: what each step looks like, and how it is drawn | `src/lib/trainingDemo.ts`, `src/ui/DemoView.tsx` |
| Real-screen spotlight, dock and layer routing | `src/ui/TrainingHost.tsx`, `src/ui/TrainingOverlay.tsx`, `src/ui/TrainingLayer.tsx`, `src/ui/Spot.tsx` |
| Practice staff, practice pass and the sign-in course | `src/lib/trainingSandbox.ts` (`practiceStaff`), `src/lib/trainingPass.ts`, `src/ui/PracticePass.tsx`, `src/training/modules/sign-in.ts` |
| Practice state and side-effect barriers | `src/state/trainingSession.ts`, `src/lib/trainingSandbox.ts`, `src/lib/trainingGuard.ts` |
| Per-staff progress | `src/lib/trainingProgress.ts`, `src/state/trainingSession.ts` |
| Page changes (new page slides in while the old one drifts away) and the dip to the page colour when practice starts or ends | `src/ui/RouteTransition.tsx`, `src/ui/Veil.tsx`, `src/lib/motion.ts` |

A course can ask for practice staff (`practiceStaff` on the course). The practice till then replaces the staff list with Casey and Morgan (built in `practiceStaff()`, with PINs hashed the same way as real ones), requires sign-in and starts signed in as Casey. A Check goal can start signed in as either, or on the Sign in screen (`staff` injection), and can cancel Morgan's pass (`pass` injection). The Scan pass window draws the practice pass while training is on (`src/ui/PracticePass.tsx`, `src/lib/trainingPass.ts`). Courses without `practiceStaff` keep the real staff list, and a `staff` injection can never lock the real till.

The starter course, **How training works**, is an engine demonstration. **Sign in, lock and switch staff** and **Build a cart** are the first task courses. More task-specific courses and device validation remain to be done. Keep each course's targets checked against the current UI spots; tests validate referenced spots and fixture IDs.

pages.title: Help home
pages.summary: How to find things in this help, and what Basic, Deep and Advanced mean.
pages.lead: This help explains every part of the POS: what each screen is for, how to do each job, what the messages mean, and what to do when something goes wrong.

sections.basic:
### Finding what you need
- Open the **Help** screen (More ▸ Help). Pages are grouped by job: selling, taking payment, the cash drawer, gift cards, orders and refunds, stock, staff, settings, and fixing problems.
- Tap the **?** in a screen header to open help for that screen. Some error alerts also have a **Help** button that opens the relevant troubleshooting page.
- Tap the **Contents** button (the list icon at the top right) to slide out the whole contents menu, like the side menu on a docs website. Sections have an arrow: tap the arrow to open or close a section, or tap a title to go to that page. The page you are on is highlighted and its sections start open. It is an extra way round: search, the trail, the lists and links all still work.
- Use the search box at the top. Type a word or two ("refund", "card declined") and every word has to match.
- A page ends with **Related pages**. Words in blue take you to another page.
- Numbered instructions are shown as separate visual steps. On the docs website, choose **Guide me through these steps** to focus on one step at a time; in the app, numbered steps are presented as distinct cards.
- For troubleshooting, start at [[fix]]. For the rules behind data, staff access and money, see [[concepts]].

### Choosing how much detail you want
Every page has up to three levels. You pick one and the Help screen remembers it.

| Level | What you get |
|---|---|
| **Basic** | What you need to know to do the job. Start here. |
| **Deep** | Basic, plus a plain-English look at how it works, so the odd behaviours make sense. |
| **Advanced** | Everything above, plus the code behind it, flowcharts, and how to trace a fault that the screen cannot fix. |

A deeper level always includes the levels above it, so you never have to read two copies of a page.

### If a page is missing or wrong
Tell the person who looks after the POS. The pages are ordinary text files, so a fix is a small edit and shows up everywhere (the app and the website) at once.
sections.deep:
### One set of pages, two places to read them
The pages are Markdown files kept in one folder. The app has a copy built in, so it works with no internet, and the docs website serves the same files. Because both read the same source, they cannot drift apart. When a page changes, its fingerprint (a short code) changes too, so a device can tell whether it has the latest.

### How pages are organised
Each page has a **parent**, which makes the folders-inside-folders shape in the website sidebar, the app's Contents menu and the topic cards in the app. Pages also point at each other with links, and each page shows the pages that link to it. Nothing is listed by hand: the contents list is built from the parents, so a new page appears in the right place the moment it exists.

### Checks before a page is accepted
A page cannot be added to the set unless its links all go somewhere, its parent exists, it has a Basic section, and its code blocks are closed. This is why you should not meet a dead link while reading.
sections.advanced:
### Where things live
| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The pages | `help/**/*.md` (a page is `help/<folder>/<name>.md`; a folder's own page is `index.md`) |
| Contents menu (rows, open sections) | `treeRows`, `openFor`, `toggled` in `src/lib/helpTree.ts`; `HelpMenu` in `src/ui/HelpMenu.tsx`; opened by the Contents button in `Help` in `src/screens/Help.tsx` |
| Format, parsing, checks, search | `src/lib/helpDocs.ts` (pure, no React) |
| Build and check script | `scripts/build-help.ts` (`npm run help:build`, `npm run help:check`) |
| What the app and the website read | `help/help.json` (generated, do not edit by hand) |
| Tests | `tests/helpdocs.test.ts` |
| Notes for people writing pages | `help/README.md` |

### The page format
A page is a header, an optional lead, and up to three sections:

```text
---
id: sales/cart-and-prices
```
